Victory to you, O Blessed Goddess! Salutations to the Giver of Boons! Victory to the Destroyer of Sin, the Bestower of Abundant Fruit! Victory to the one who holds the skulls of Śumbha and Niśumbha; I bow down to you, the Remover of the Suffering of Gods and Men! 103.

Victory to you who bear the moon and sun as eyes! Victory to you whose excellent face is adorned by fire! Victory to you who are absorbed within the body of Bhairava! Victory to you who dry up the blood of Andhaka! 104.

Victory to you, O crusher of Mahiṣa, who holds a trident in your hand; victory to you, the remover of all the sins of the world! Victory, O Goddess, saluted by Brahmā and Rāma; victory, you who are bowed to by the Sun and Indra! 105.

Victory to you, who are praised by the six-faced Lord armed with weapons; victory to you, who flow through the ocean and are praised by Śambhu! Victory to you, the destroyer of the poverty of suffering; victory to you, the increaser of sons and wives! 106.

Victory, O Goddess, bearer of all bodies; victory, O revealer of heaven, remover of suffering! Victory, O destroyer of disease, bestower of liberation; victory, O giver of desires, supreme among the perfected ones! 107
Whoever recites this hymn composed by Vyāsa in the presence of Śiva, or at home with a pure disposition, free from desire and anger—108.
Vyāsa will be pleased with him, and the one whose vehicle is the bull (Śiva) will be pleased; the goddess Narmadā, who causes the destruction of all sins, will also be pleased.
Those by whom the Narmadā has been praised on earth do not go to the realm of Yama; O Goddess, even the Grandfather (Brahmā) would be bewildered by the chanting of your virtues.
O Narmadā, even Vākpati himself does not know your true nature; O Goddess, how could I venture to know your qualities? (111)
Having thus recognized his pure disposition through the actions of speech, mind, and body, the goddess Narmadā became pleased and then spoke these words: (112)
"O Vyāsa, O great sage! I am pleased by your truthful speech; whatever boon you desire, I shall grant it all to you. (113)
Vyāsa said: "O Goddess, if you are pleased with me, and if a boon is to be granted to me, you ought to grant hospitality to the sages on the northern bank."
Narmadā said: "O Vyāsa, what you have requested is improper—the setting forth upon a wrong path. Even Indra, Candra, and Yama would not be able to set out upon a deviant course."
"Ask for another boon, my son, whatever may be difficult to obtain on earth. Having heard these words of the goddess, Vyāsa then fell into a swoon.
Thinking, "Today my affliction has become in vain," he fell down; the entire earth, along with its mountains, forests, and groves, trembled. || 117 ||
Then, seeing Vyāsa fallen into a swoon, all the gods, including Indra, arrived there by the thousands with cries of "Alas! Alas! on their lips. || 118 ||
They raised up Vyāsa, who was devoted to the study of the Vedas; he had exerted himself for the sake of the Brahmins and not for his own sake, O best of rivers.
"For the sake of cows and for the sake of Brahmins, one should immediately renounce one's life; thus was Narmadā proclaimed by Brahmā and the other foremost of the gods. (120)
Terrified, Revā sprinkled him with her own water and many very cool breezes; and Satyavatī’s son, having regained consciousness, bowed to the gods and spoke to the river.

Vyāsa said: "O Goddess, it is said that the fruit of serving all the sacred fords has been ordained for me; yet, due to my misfortune, my hope for merit has become as fruitless as forest flowers are to common people. (122)
Narmadā said: "O noble one, wherever on this earth you wish to lead me, today I shall follow behind you, O wielder of the staff, along your path together with the Vindhya mountain. (123)
Thus addressed, the highly effulgent Vyāsa, son of Satyavatī, caused the best of rivers to move toward the south of his own hermitage.
The sage of great splendor, staff in hand, uttered the syllable "huṃ"; terrified by Vyāsa’s "huṃ," that daughter of Rudra trembled.
Pointing out the way with his staff, the goddess proceeded there; having entered the path of Vyāsa, the goddess was seen by those led by Śakra.
Then the gods, together with their attendants, released a rain of flowers, saying: "Tell us, my son, what shall we do? We have been delighted by your deed. (127)
Vyāsa said: Having performed extensive austerity and having given gifts of great fruit, this alone should be done by men—that which brings happiness to the virtuous. (128)
"If you, O highly fortunate ones, are pleased, and if I am indeed worthy of your favor, then let all of you stay in my hermitage; there is no doubt about this. (129)

This hospitality, consisting of leafy vegetables mixed with the waters of the Revā, has been accepted by all of you, headed by Parāśara. All of you must remain in your own hermitage on the northern bank of the Revā.
Mārkaṇḍeya said: After the daily rites of bathing and libations had been performed by the best of the twice-born, they all went to Vyāsakuṇḍa and offered oblations there.
Gautama, Bhṛgu, Māṇḍavya, Nārada, and likewise Lomaśa offered oblations into the sacred fire with bilva fruits and bilva leaves.
Parāśara, as well as Śaṅkha, Kauśika, the sage Cyavana, Pippalāda, Vasiṣṭha, and Nāciketa of great asceticism; || 133 ||
Viśvāmitra and Agastya, as well as Uddālaka and Yama; Śāṇḍilya, Jaimini, Kaṇva, Yājñavalkya, Aśana, and Aṅgiras. || 134 ||
Śātātapa and Dadhīci, Kapila and Gālava, as well as Jaigīṣavya, Dakṣa, Bharata, and Mudgala. || 135 ||
Vātsyāyana of great splendor, Saṃvarta, Śakti, Jātūkarṇya, Bharadvāja, as well as the Vālakhilyas and Aruṇi; || 136 ||
Thousands such as these offer oblations into the fire, their fingers marked by rosaries and devoted to the yoga of meditation.
Then all the twice-born, with one-pointed minds, performed the rite of oblation; thereupon, a Liṅga arose, which bestows liberation and destroys disease.
Having beheld the supreme, indestructible God, Vyāsa was filled with joy; the gods showered flowers, and the best of the twice-born offered their blessings. (139)
Having seen the three-eyed God, Vyāsa prostrated himself with the eight limbs; he then honored the Brahmins with vegetables, roots, and fruits.
O son of Pāṇḍu, all the twice-born were first fed by his father; then, having bestowed their auspicious blessings, the brahmins departed once more. (141)
From that time onwards, that sacred site has been called Vyāsa by the wise.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: Tell me all the merit of Vyāsatīrtha, as well as the rules for bathing and giving gifts there, and at what time it yields great fruit. (143)
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: O Pāṇḍava, together with your brothers, I shall tell you everything regarding the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Kārttika; one should remain with senses subdued.
The man who, having observed the fast with devotion, keeps a vigil at night, should devoutly bathe the Lord with honey, milk, and clarified butter.
Furthermore, one should smear the Supreme Lord with curd mixed with sugar, with water infused with *kuśa* grass, and with fragrant sandalwood paste.
Then one should worship with fragrant flowers, bilva leaves, mucukunda, kunda, and jasmine blossoms. || 147 ||
One should worship the unsurpassed Lord of the Island with the utmost devotion, using *unmatta* and *munipuṣpa* flowers, as well as others that bloom in season. (148)
The Supreme Lord is pleased by the gift of a jar of sugarcane juice; by the gift of eight jars, even powerful sin is destroyed. (149)
And [the merit] earned in a month is destroyed by eight hundred [recitations], that of six months by a thousand, and likewise that of a year by two thousand.
Sins accumulated since birth are destroyed by ten thousand [repetitions]; diseases are destroyed by double that number, and by triple that number, there shall be the acquisition of wealth. (151)
By six qualities one becomes eloquent, and by twice that number one likewise becomes a Siddha; by ten lakhs [of recitations], the state of Rudra is attained—of this there is no doubt. (152)
O best of kings, on the full moon day one should perform a bath with devotion according to the procedure prescribed by the mantras, which brings about the destruction of all sins. (153)
The wise man should duly gratify the gods, the ancestors, and human beings with the Vāruṇa, Āgneya, and Brāhma offerings, which bring about inexhaustible results.

Through the *ṛc* verse one obtains the merit born of the *Ṛgveda*, through the *sāman* chant the fruit of the *Sāmaveda*, and through the *yajus* formula of the *Yajurveda* or by means of the *Gāyatrī*, one may attain everything. || 155 ||
One should mutter the imperishable mantra, whether it be that of the Sun, or one dedicated to Śiva, or else the Vaiṣṇava mantra known as the twelve-syllabled one. 156.
One should worship with devotion those brāhmaṇas who are endowed with all auspicious marks, who are devoted to their own wives, who are learned, and who are free from hypocrisy and greed. (157)
Those who cause the breaking of conduct, the wicked, the fallen, those who serve Śūdras, those engaged in taking a Śūdra woman as a wife, and he in whose house there is a Vṛṣalī; || 158 ||
Those who speak behind one's back, those intent on reviling wicked teachers, those whose nature is to hate the Vedas, the rationalists, and those who act like herons (hypocrites). || 159 ||
One should avoid such persons at a śrāddha, in giving gifts, and in all religious observances; better is a Brahmin who is well-restrained, even if he knows only the essence of the Gāyatrī. (160)
One who is unrestrained, though learned in the four Vedas, who eats all things and sells all things—such Brahmins one should honor with gifts of food, grain, and gold. (161)
He who gives sandals, garments, a bed, an umbrella, or a seat to a brāhmaṇa with devotion is also glorified in heaven. (162)
In that [rite], a fragrant water-cow and likewise a ghee-cow should be presented visibly; furthermore, a sesame-cow and buffaloes should also be given.
He who is a giver of a black antelope skin, he who is a giver of sesame seeds and clarified butter, and he who is a giver of a maiden and a book—such a person shall attain the imperishable world.
One who desires heaven should cause to be given two draft-oxen, equipped with hooves and provided with grain and household utensils; this is my truthful declaration. (165)
One should encircle the island or the auspicious altar with a thread, or else the temple or the Supreme Lord with supreme devotion. (166)
O King, that man who performs a circumambulation here according to the prescribed rite [attains the merit of] the islands named Jambū and Plakṣa, as well as the other, Śālmali. (167)
Kuśa, Krauñca, as well as Kāśa, and Puṣkara as the seventh—by these, O Bhārata, [the earth] is surrounded up to the seven oceans.
O Great King, lord of the island, one should cause the ritual release of a bull (vṛṣotsarga) to be performed; by means of a reddish-colored bull, one shall attain the world of Maheśa.
He who indeed has white [marks] on the face, the forehead, and likewise on the feet, and he whose tail is white—he indeed is the one who shows the way to heaven.
O Bhārata, this Nīla mountain is described as being of such a nature; he who would abandon his life on the lord of islands dwells in heaven for as many years as there are hairs on his body.
O King, by the power of Vyāsatīrtha, he enjoys the worlds of Sūrya, Śaṅkara, Brahmā, and Viṣṇu in succession according to his own will. (172)
Then, one should worship the brahmin there with devotion along with his wife; whoever gives white and red garments to that foremost of the twice-born [shall obtain merit]. (173)
Having performed a circumambulation of the pair [of deities], let the Teacher of the World be pleased with me; there is no kinsman equal to a Brahmin in this world and in the next. (174)
He who protects one falling into the most terrible world of Yama—namely, one who knows the Itihāsas and Purāṇas, is a devotee of Viṣṇu, and has conquered his senses. || 175 ||
One should worship with supreme devotion, especially a singer of the Sāman hymns; and those who, remaining at home, remember Dvīpeśvara with devotion.
For them, no grief arises, nor loss, nor any ill-deed; one should first worship the Liṅga there, and thereafter Siddheśvara. || 177 ||
There, the illustrious Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, attained perfection; it was by worshipping this very place that the high-minded Dhārāsarpa became a perfected one. || 178 ||
O King, whoever gives up their life at that sacred ford pierces through the world of the Sun and goes into the presence of Śiva.

O Bhārata, one indeed dwells for seven thousand years in water, eleven thousand in fire, sixteen thousand in falling [from a height], sixty thousand in a great battle, and eighty thousand in the seizure of cattle; but by fasting unto death, there is an imperishable state.
The father, the grandfather, and likewise the great-grandfather, having become wind, behold their own kinsman approaching. (181)
"In our lineage, is there any son who would offer us water with sesame seeds, especially on the full moon day of Kārttika and likewise on that of Vaiśākha? (182)
"And by resorting to that sacred site (tīrtha), we shall attain the heavenly realm. Thus, everything concerning this unsurpassed Dvīpeśvara has been told to you. (183)
O King, whoever should recite this with supreme devotion or listen to it with a mind fixed upon it, shall also be liberated from sin and rejoice in the abode of Śiva.
O best of kings, there is no doubt that Vyāsatīrtha, created by the preeminent sages, is the salt-waste of all holy fords and the granter of all desires. (185)
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thereafter, O king of kings, one should go to the most excellent Prabhāseśvara, renowned throughout the three worlds as the supreme staircase to heaven. || 1 ||
Yudhiṣṭhira said: "O dear one, tell me how Prabhāsa originated and how it yields great fruit; describe to me briefly that visible place which provides a staircase to heaven."
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: The unfortunate wife of the Sun, renowned by the name Prabhā, formerly propitiated Śambhu through severe penance.
Subsisting on air alone, she remained devoted to meditation for year after year; then, O son of Pāṇḍu, Mahādeva was pleased with Prabhā.
Īśvara said: "O young woman, why do you grieve? Tell me what you wish to say; for I am indeed the one Bhāskara, and no multiplicity exists at all."
The Lord said: "O Lord Śambhu, for a woman there is no other god anywhere than her husband—whether he be possessed of qualities or devoid of them, wealthy or destitute. (6)

Whether beloved or even hated, the husband alone is the deity of women. O Lord of the Gods, scorched by my misfortune, I suffer intensely because I have obtained such happiness from my husband in the midst of my friends.
Īśvara said: "By my grace, you shall indeed become beloved of the Sun."
Pārvatī said: "Your word shall not go unheeded; even Bhāskara will act accordingly. O Supreme Lord, otherwise this Prabhā would suffer in vain."
At the word of Umā, the Sun—the destroyer of the darkness within Maheśāna—descended from the sky onto the northern bank of the Narmadā.
Bhānu said: "O Lord, O destroyer of the demon Aghāsura, why have I been summoned?"
Īśvara said: "O Bhānu, protect Prabhā indeed with supreme contentment."
Umā said: "O Destroyer of Snow, may you dwell eternally in the palace of Prabhā; O Ravi, may she be made the foremost wife among all your consorts. (13)
Bhānu said: "O Goddess, O lady of lovely countenance, I shall do exactly as you have commanded. Having heard this, Prabhā, being summoned, replied to Maheśvara.
The Lord said: "O God, O Enemy of Manmatha, O Lord of Umā, remain here with one portion of yourself; let another portion be established here for the manifestation of this sacred ford."
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: O Pāṇḍava, a Liṅga consisting of all the gods was established there, renowned as Prabhāseśa, which is difficult to find in all the worlds. (16)
Other holy places indeed bear fruit in due time, O king of kings; but Prabhāseśa grants the fruits of one's desires instantly.
O King, on the seventh day of the bright fortnight of the month of Māgha, especially so, he who should touch the horse there before a Brāhmaṇa as prescribed; || 18 ||
By that [act], the status of Indra or the station of the Sun is attained; having bathed with supreme devotion, one should give a gift to a twice-born man.
O Lord of the Best, the giver of a cow shall attain heaven and Satyaloka, [receiving] a beautiful, radiant, young, and auspicious milch-cow with limbs lovely in every part.
O best of kings, those who give away a cow together with her calf, equipped with a bell and yielding milk into a bronze vessel, do not go to the abode of Yama.
Now, he who causes the bath of the God to be performed with supreme devotion attains the highest world for as long as the dissolution of all beings.
O Pāṇḍava, misfortune comes to an end merely by bathing there; moreover, he who with devotion bestows the gift of a maiden at that sacred site [attains great merit]. (23)

O son of Pāṇḍu, one should cause her to be given to a Brāhmaṇa through the marriage rite; she should be given to one of similar age, and likewise endowed with noble lineage, good character, and wealth.
O Great King, even those who are burdened with sins, when they give [gifts], their evils dissolve just as salt dissolves in water. (25)
The sin committed by betraying one's master, that of one who misappropriates a deposit, and that which arises from false testimony accrue to the betrayer of a friend and the ungrateful person.
The sin arising from the destruction of that village's groves, the sin of consorting with another's wife, the sin of a usurer, and the sin born of theft— [all these he takes upon himself]. (27)

That which arises from breaking a well, that of one who observes the "vow of a cat," that which is hypocritical, that born from cutting down trees, and that produced by the prohibition of marriage; 28.
[The sin] arising from cutting down trees in a grove, from approaching those who should not be approached, from abandoning one's own wife, and from the desire for another's wife; (29)

Whatever sin arises from seizing the property of a Brahmin, from administering poison, from killing a cow, from the sale of sacred knowledge, and whatever sin results from association [with the wicked]. || 30 ||

The terrible sin arising from the killing of a dog or a cat, as well as that born from a snake or a Śūdra, and whatever sin belongs to one who seizes land, as well as to the one who causes the seizure of land; (31)
O Pāṇḍava, whatever sin exists in saying "do not give" regarding cows, fire, or Brahmins—that sin goes to destruction through the gift of a daughter in marriage.
Having gone to the world of Bhāskara, he shall proceed to the auspicious world of Rudra; staying in the world of Rudra, he sports there for as long as the fourteen Indras endure.
When the destruction of all sins has occurred, O son of Pāṇḍu, this meditation arises for one who goes to the auspicious holy site of Prabhāsa. (34)

Having obtained the fruit of all sacred fords (tīrthas), he shall attain the fruit of the horse sacrifice (aśvamedha). The gift of a cow is of great merit, the supreme destroyer of all sins; it is indeed recommended at all times, and especially on the fourteenth day (caturdaśī).
Chapter 99
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thereafter, O protector of the earth, one should go to Vāsukīśa, established on the southern bank of the Narmadā, which destroys the entire multitude of sins.
Yudhiṣṭhira said: For what reason, O dear one, was Vāsukīśa installed on the southern bank of the Revā? Tell me in detail, O Teacher. (2)
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having established all this, Śambhu indeed performed the dance.
From his exertion, sweat was born, which, mixed with the waters of the Gaṅgā as it fell forth from the crest of Hara’s head, was consumed by the serpent.
Then Mandākinī, filled with rage, said over the snake, "O Bhārata, O wretched creature, you shall indeed attain the state of a python, O serpent! (5)

Vāsuki said: "I am a sinner and a wicked person who deserves your favor, for there is no one other than Hara [to do so]. You are a river of auspicious characteristics, meritorious and the purifier of the three worlds."
For you are the one who severs the cycle of existence and destroys the suffering of the afflicted; you indeed stand at the gateway to heaven—O Sovereign Goddess, have mercy upon me!
Gangā said: "Perform extensive penance directed toward Śaṅkara on the Vindhya mountain; then, by my command, you shall regain your own place and your state as a serpent."
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: Then that serpent, having quickly gone to the auspicious Vindhya mountain, began to perform penance, intent upon the propitiation of Śaṅkara.

"Choose a boon from me, my child, O serpent, for you have shown me honor."

Vāsuki said: "If you are pleased with me, O God, and will grant a boon, O Śaṅkara, then by your grace, O Lord of Gods, may freedom from sin be mine. Please describe some sacred ford (tīrtha) that destroys all sins. (12)
The Lord said: "O mighty-armed serpent, go to the auspicious Revā; perform your bath according to the prescribed rites on its meritorious southern bank."
Having spoken thus, the god vanished; Vāsuki, filled with haste, entered the waters of the Narmadā in the form of a python.
By that path, the supreme stream of the Jāhnavī was produced; the serpent, his impurities shaken off, was born in the waters of the Narmadā.
Śaṅkara was established there on the Narmadā, O Yudhiṣṭhira; thereafter is the famous Nāgeśvara Liṅga, which destroys all sins.
On the eighth or the fourteenth lunar day, one should bathe Śiva with honey; he immediately becomes freed from all taint—of this there is no doubt.
O Pārtha, those men who are childless and perform their ablutions at the confluence obtain excellent and auspicious sons, equal to Kārtavīrya.
O prince, he who, devoted to fasting, performs a śrāddha ceremony at that very place, shall liberate the deceased ancestors from hell by doing so.
No fear of serpents arises within his lineage or circle of kinsmen; by the grace of the Nāgas, his family prospers, free from all harm.
All this has been told to you out of affection, O best of kings.
Chapter 100
Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thereafter, O protector of the earth, one should go to the most splendid holy site known as Mārkaṇḍeśa, located on the southern bank of the Narmadā.
O son, this is the most excellent of all holy places, auspicious and worshipped by the gods; it is more secret than the secret, and has not been told by me to anyone else.
Formerly, I established that knowledge which is like a staircase to heaven; and it was there itself that knowledge arose within me through the grace of Śaṅkara.
Furthermore, O son of Pāṇḍu, anyone else who goes there and recites the Drupadā mantra while submerged in the water is liberated from all sins without exception.
Even by means of verbal, mental, or bodily sins, he remains stationed in the southern direction, supporting himself upon the pedestal.
One should devotedly unite with the trident-bearer of thirty-two forms; upon the fall of the body, one shall go to Śiva—this is my certainty, O King.
O Bhārata, one should awaken the lamp with clarified butter on the night of the eighth day; thus Śaṅkara has declared that one attains the heavenly world.
O prince, if one performs a śrāddha there with devotion, his ancestors remain satisfied until the dissolution of all beings.
Whoever offers libations there with inguda, badara, or bilva fruits, or with unbroken rice grains (akṣata) or water, shall obtain for his ancestors the fruit of their births.
Chapter 101

Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya said: Thereafter, O king of kings, one should go to a most beautiful holy site (tīrtha) located on the northern bank of the Narmadā, in the middle of the sacrificial enclosure (yajñavāṭa).
Known on earth as Saṃkarṣaṇa, it is the destroyer of sins; O King, in ancient times, Balabhadra indeed performed penance there.
O prince, even the gods were present right there; Śambhu was stationed in that very place together with Umā, as was Keśava.
