Nothing at all was given by me in the past, nor was an oblation offered into the fire; no protection was afforded to the world, nor were those who sought refuge saved. (50)
"Whatever jewel I have seen or not seen upon the surface of the earth, all of that has indeed been taken by me by force from all embodied beings here. (51)
Then, after a long time, my kingdom was forcibly seized by my own son, who banished me in disgrace once I was overcome by old age.
Then, seized by old age and having attained supreme detachment, O best of Brahmins, I arrived here while wandering hither and thither.
Then, with my throat parched by hunger, having bathed here in these auspicious waters, I lay down as if dead, tormented by hunger.
Having entered this holy water, he met his death; and at that very moment, a celestial chariot appeared before him.
Then the servants, having taken me up with another body and placed me there, arrived at the abode of Brahmā.
Wearing divine garlands and excellent garments, anointed with divine perfumes, adorned with divine ornaments, and being praised by the Kinnaras.
Then, in the midst of the assembly of Brahmā, I was indeed held by those divine servants in such a form and with eyes wide open before Brahmā.
All those who were present in the assembly looked at one another with faces full of astonishment; others censured him, loudly uttering the word "Fie! (dhik). || 59 ||
The servants said: "This is the four-faced God, and this is his assembly hall, frequented by all the hosts of gods; let a salutation be made. (60)
Then, having prostrated deeply before that god who was accompanied by the gods, I sat down in the midst of the assembly, standing with my head bowed in shame.
O Pot-born One, whatever discourses concerning the gods, the twice-born, and kings, as well as narrations on dharma, were produced there upon the floor of that assembly hall.
In such a manner, my hunger increases excessively; I wonder what I shall eat quickly—perhaps even stones or wood? (63)
Then, having cast shame far away, I bowed down and prostrated myself before my great-grandfather, the best of sages, and addressed him with loud words. (64)
"O Great-Grandfather, hunger afflicts me exceedingly at this moment; I do not see anything of that sort to eat, so grant me some food. (65)
"Indeed, those defects such as hunger and thirst do not exist here for one staying in heaven; how is it that this is so for me? (66)
The Grandfather said: "O evil-minded one, you have never given food to anyone anywhere on the surface of the earth; therefore, even here, your hunger continues to increase."
Likewise, those jewels which were seen by you have been taken away; consequently, even though I have entered into my world, I am born devoid of sight.
"Since you, though burdened with sin, have arrived at my abode, I shall tell you all of that; listen with a focused mind. (69)
O sinful soul, in that water where you gave up your life-breaths, the Lord of Śvetadvīpa dwells, afflicted by the fear of the Kali age.
Then, by the mere touch of him, he was instantly liberated from all sins; yet, from eating his food, a supreme suffering arising from hunger was produced. (71)
Likewise, this blindness of yours arose from the theft of jewels; there is no other cause whatsoever. This which I have spoken is the truth.
Then, O best of the twice-born, I again declared the ritual procedure: "This world of Brahmā is even superior to hell; therefore, O Lord, send me to that very place—what need is there for this? (73)
Brahmā said: Therefore, go to that very place; why indeed have you been sent here? Your dwelling shall not be in hell, but rather in the Śvetadvīpa.
The majesty of a scripture perishes when it is devoid of truth; therefore, you shall always remain mounted upon this most beautiful celestial chariot.
"Go to that reservoir where you gave up your life, and eat your own body there according to your desire. (76)
By my word, that [food] situated in the midst of the water shall become inexhaustible; and your vision shall remain fixed upon it for as long as the time of eating lasts.
Then, by his word, I always come here at midnight on the day of the Festival of Lamps and devour my own body. (78)
Then I attain satisfaction for as long as a divine day remains, and likewise for a human year; such is the state in which I abide. (79)
O best of sages, there is nothing whatsoever in the three worlds that is impossible for you to accomplish, since you once took the entire ocean in a single handful and drank it.
Therefore, O Sage, having shown me the greatest compassion, deliver me from this state which is censured by all the world. (81)
"Likewise, O best of sages, grant me the gift of sight; I am weary of this state of blindness, and there is no other refuge for me but you. (82)
Having heard those words of his, my mind then melted with compassion, O best of the Raghus, and I spoke these words to him.
"Give me the price for food: this ornament here upon my neck, by which this hunger arising in my belly may come to an end. (84)
Likewise, O wise one, from this day forward, give very pure jewel-lamps right here on the shore of this lake to Dāmodara as well. (85)
By this truth, may that stainless, eternal vision which arises for you from my words be born; I swear this truly by my own self, free from all doubt. (86)
The king said: O best of sages, having shown compassion toward me, you yourself accept this excellent necklace composed of jewels from my neck. (87)

Then, overcome by compassion, I accepted his gift; though free from desire and dwelling in the forest, I, a sage, accepted it. Thereupon, having washed my feet, he—whose soul was purified by true devotion—gave me this ornament as the price for the food, O King. At that very moment, his hunger vanished, and a supreme satisfaction arose within him, born of divine nectar.
His destroyed and dead body, as well as that which had arisen before him and was decaying, remained established in that water which was imperishable and eternal.
Then, O best of the Raghus, having constructed an excellent temple, Dāmodara was installed with great devotion by him in that place. (92)
To whatever extent one endowed with faith offers a lamp before him, to that same extent his vision shall become eternally and perfectly pure.
Then, after one month had passed, that lord of the earth attained divine vision; he became the best of kings, most desirable to the virtuous.
Then, having prostrated with joined palms, he spoke to me joyfully in a voice faltering with delight as he set out toward heaven: || 95 ||
"By your grace, O best of Brahmins, my most terrible hunger has been destroyed, and likewise, divine vision has arisen within me. (96)
Therefore, grant me permission, O best of sages, so that by the power of this sacred ford (tīrtha), I may go at once to the world of Brahmā.
Then, having been released by me and bowing down again and again, he departed with a joyful heart for the eternal world of Brahmā. 98.
"In this way, this ornament previously came into my possession; knowing it to be worthy of you, I have presented it to you. (99)

From that time onwards, O Indra among kings, men who come here and offer radiant jewel-lamps after bathing in these auspicious waters during the month of Kārtika, depart for the abode of the gods at the end of their physical life.
Furthermore, O best of the Raghus, those who, being composed in mind, give up their lives—even if they are evil-souled—go to the world of Brahmā.
Then, having seen the power arising from that water, the thousand-eyed Indra, overwhelmed with fear, filled it completely on all sides with dust.
Today the day has arrived that gives rise to the Festival of Lights; it is most meritorious here, so by my command, you must construct a fine small well.
Having performed your bath therein, O Rāghava, then offer libations to the ancestors; place an unsurpassed jewel-lamp before this deity.
By this [means], the accomplishment that arises from the world of Brahmā is attained; with this very body, this truth has been spoken by me. (5)
Then, by the command of Rāghava, all those Rākṣasas and Vānaras placed a well of pure water in that place.
Having bathed there, offered libations to the ancestors, and presented jewel-lamps, they then set out for Ayodhyā, continuing thus throughout the entire month of Kārttika.
Then, leaving behind Vibhīṣaṇa and the monkey Hanumān, they all went to the world of Brahmā by the power of that sacred ford.

Sūta said: Even today, whoever respectfully offers a lamp there, having bathed in those auspicious waters when the month of Kārttika has arrived, is liberated from all sins and is glorified in the world of Brahmā. (109)
Thus, that auspicious Tattaḍāga was produced there, as well as the Ānarttīya [tank] and that beautiful Viṣṇukūpikā.
The sages said: O Sūta, proclaim the greatness of those liṅgas which were installed there by the Rākṣasas endowed with devotion.
Sūta said: For the sake of their worship, fierce and exceedingly powerful Rākṣasas used to come from the city of Laṅkā by the hundreds in ancient times.
Coming and going on that path and in that field, they devour the multitudes of people, including both children and the elderly. (3)
Then all those men, fleeing in every direction, ran hither and thither, intent on saving their lives.
Likewise, many others, having gone to the great city named Ayodhyā, spoke to Kuśa, the son of Rāma and best of kings, while being deeply distressed. || 5 ||
O King, those Rākṣasas who previously arrived together with your father in the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara, led by Vibhīṣaṇa— [6]
Indeed, four-faced Liṅgas were installed there by the lords of the Rākṣasas with their own mantras in the western part of that sacred field.
And by that very same association, they constantly come together; likewise, in that sacred field, they carry out the devouring of the world.
If any man were to worship those lingas, he would meet with immediate destruction; that too became a great calamity.
Therefore, O Lord of the Earth, if you do not provide us protection, then this entire world will surely and gradually go to its destruction.
And that field was especially [holy], for it was there that those Rākṣasas of cruel deeds, who were ever greedy for human flesh, used to come.
Having heard that, the king immediately informed his ministers; then, accompanied by his army, he went there to assume the burden of the kingdom.
Then, seeing that Kuśa had arrived, the remaining best of the twice-born rebuked him with words of harsh syllables and spoke to him.
Why do you rule the kingdom in such a manner, O lowest of Kṣatriyas, that you bring about its destruction while the people are being carried off by Rākṣasas? (14)
Surely you were not born from Rāma, but rather from Rāvaṇa, since you look on with indifference while we are all being tormented by the Rākṣasas.
This is true, as was stated of old by those expert in the treatises on ethics: "Whichever caste has a king of its own, that caste prospers in happiness. (16)
Therefore, having arisen as a Rākṣasa, you neglect all those best of the twice-born and others who are being devoured by Rākṣasas. || 17 ||
Where tears fall upon the surface of the earth from afflicted people due to the faults arising from the king, there the king partakes in that fault. (18)
Kuśa said: "O Brahmins, let favor be shown to me; I was not aware that such a defeat of the Brahmins had arisen from the Rākṣasas. (19)
From this day forward, whoever shall be brought to destruction anywhere—whether a Brāhmaṇa or anyone else—that shall be my own sin. (20)
Having spoken thus, Rāghava, filled with rage, then quickly dispatched a messenger free from fear to Vibhīṣaṇa.
Go, messenger, and having gone quickly, Vibhīṣaṇa is to be told by you: "A great affection worthy of Rāma has been shown by you toward me."
O evil-minded one, having gained my trust with your fair words, you now afflict me along with the hosts of rākṣasas on every side throughout this land.
"O lowest of Rākṣasas, this installation of yours was performed by my father; therefore, I shall slay you just as your brother was struck down by our father. (24)
Even a poison tree, once it has been brought to growth by one's own self, how can it be cut down here by the wise? (25)
Therefore, from this day forward, if any night-stalker should somehow reach the northern shore of the ocean, [he shall be slain]. (26)
Therefore, having quickly reached this city of yours, Laṅkā, I shall, together with my army, destroy it as well as all the night-stalkers.
And having bound you with firm snares and well-restrained with fetters, I shall place you in prison this very instant; of this there is no doubt. (28)
Having been addressed thus, the messenger then went quickly to the bridge; and having seen the god Rāmeśvara, he stood before him.
Then he was asked by some people: "Who are you, child, who have come here? For what purpose? Tell us, for no men go here. (30)
The messenger said: "I have been sent by King Kuśa to the house of Vibhīṣaṇa for a specific purpose; how shall I go there?"
The people said: "No man whatsoever is able to go beyond this from now on, because the bridge was broken in the middle by Rāma, whose actions are effortless."
Therefore, O messenger, your mission shall achieve success right here; for everything will be accomplished by Vibhīṣaṇa through his mere sight of that Rākṣasa.
At all times, this lord of the Rākṣasas, having undertaken a strict vow, worships the three auspicious forms of Rāmeśvara during the three periods of the day.
Vibhīṣaṇa himself performs worship at dawn for that Maheśvara who stands at the gateway of Laṅkā upon the section of the bridge.
And as for that second fragment of the bridge situated in the midst of the water, one should worship Rāmeśvara located there at midday.
O King, by always coming at midnight and worshipping him with devotion, one shall undoubtedly attain success; this which has been proclaimed is the truth. (37)
Therefore, remain unperturbed and composed right here in this place until the arrival of that great-souled Rākṣasa. (38)
Afterwards, accompanied by him alone, you shall go at your own will either to his palace or to your own home, once you have been dismissed by him.
Then, having heard that from them, the messenger, filled with joy, said "So be it," and remained right there.
Then, when midnight had arrived, Vibhīṣaṇa, surrounded by Rākṣasas, came to that auspicious sanctuary.
Mounted upon an excellent celestial chariot, he was being praised from all sides by those Rākṣasas in the form of bards, as well as by others who were singing his praises.
Having descended from his excellent celestial chariot and performed three circumambulations, he bowed deeply to Rāmeśvara and uttered this hymn of praise.
Salutations to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, bestower of fearlessness upon your devotees! Your hands and feet are everywhere; your eyes, heads, and faces are on all sides.
You are the sacrifice, you are the exclamation Vaṣaṭ; you are the moon, you are the maker of light. You are Viṣṇu, you are the four-faced one, you are Śakra, and you are the Supreme Lord.
Just as oil always remains hidden within sesame seeds, so do you, O Śaṅkara, remain hidden within all the worlds. 495.
Just as fire residing within wood is not perceived even though it is present, so too you are not perceived by the deluded, even though you abide everywhere.
Just as clarified butter exists within curd in a hidden state, so, O God, do you abide within all beings, both moving and unmoving. 48.
Just as a man obtains water by digging from the surface of the earth, so too one who worships you constantly attains liberation without a doubt. (49)
Heaven is so difficult to attain, and enemies are so formidable, as long as you do not bring contentment to embodied beings. 50.
So long does the fortune of men remain unstable, and so long do various diseases persist, O God of gods, as you do not attain complete satisfaction.
O Lord, as long as you do not bestow contentment upon embodied beings here, so long will there exist the suffering arising from sons, as well as that arising from beloved ones.
Having thus offered praise, he then bathed the Liṅga according to the prescribed rite and subsequently massaged it with divine fragrant ointments.
And with *pārijātaka* flowers, as well as those produced from the *santāna* tree, those arising from the *kalpa* trees, and likewise those born of the *mandāra* tree. (54)
Endowed with supreme faith, he performed a very extensive worship; having first adorned [the image] with divine ornaments, he then [adorned it] with divine garments.
And he himself sang the song, keeping time with his hand—a beautiful melody fashioned with rhythmic modulations and adorned with the seven notes.
Endowed with those logical arguments and well-adorned with villages and melodies, having acted thus, he performed service to that deity with devotion. (57)
Just as Vibhīṣaṇa was setting out once more toward Laṅkā, a messenger stood before him and spoke these words of Kuśa.
In particular, however, that which was previously spoken by him in his presence—when he was overcome by extreme anger and his eyes were bloodshot—[is as follows]. (59)
Having heard that, Vibhīṣaṇa, standing bowed in humility with his palms joined in reverence, prostrated deeply and spoke loudly to the messenger.
If it is thus that the kingdom has been established for Rāma’s son by the Rākṣasas, then surely all of that has been accomplished by me, O best of messengers.
Therefore, great favor has been shown to me by that high-souled one, since you have been sent by Kuśa into the presence of my fool.
Having spoken thus, he purified all those Rākṣasas who, having gone to the surface of the earth, were indeed constantly destroying mortals.
Then, having brought them right there into the presence of that messenger, he spoke thus to each of them individually, shedding tears out of anger.
By those evil-minded Rākṣasas, who have reached the kingdom of my high-souled lord Kuśa, the destruction of people has been wrought. (65)
May all those fierce Vyaṃtaras, constantly afflicted by hunger and thirst, become utterly miserable as they stand at the gates of Laṅkā.
Having renounced all enjoyments, they endure cold and heat; subsisting on phlegm, urine, and excrement, they are despised by all people. (67)
Having thus pronounced that curse upon them, the best of Rākṣasas then spoke again to the messenger with his palms joined in reverence.

"From this day forward, no Rākṣasa shall approach us. Therefore, O Kuśa, you must speak on my behalf to that best of the Raghus, saying: 'May my transgression be forgiven, for this was done by me out of ignorance.'"
O messenger, you have witnessed with your own eyes how those of the wicked race of Rākṣasas, who were greedy for human flesh, were subdued by me.
Whatever other task there may be, whether divine or human, all of that must be told to me, your servant, without hesitation. (71)
The messenger said: "O Rākṣasa, go there yourself quickly and uproot those Liṅgas which have been fashioned by the Rākṣasas. (72)
This alone is the supreme task that brings happiness to all the world; and those [images] which have been installed with mantras originating from the Rākṣasas.
O Rākṣasa, if some human, unaware that these four-faced [liṅgas] are worshipped by the Rākṣasas, should perform worship to them, [he would meet with misfortune]. (74)

It perishes at that very moment; this has been witnessed by me personally. For this reason, O Lord of Rākṣasas, I tell you: as long as those Liṅgas remain upon the earth, all the night-stalkers shall remain established. (75)
Vibhīṣaṇa said: "Indeed, I previously made a vow in the presence of Rāma: 'Having passed beyond Rāmeśvara, I shall not go further upon this earth. (76)
Furthermore, O messenger, another reason has been stated here by the wise: one should not move a Śiva-liṅga, whether it be situated poorly or well. (77)
Therefore, how can I go there and effect a division of the Liṅga, having myself become a devotee of Maheśvara and having personally made this vow? (78)
Therefore, that lord of men should be propitiated by you through my words; whatever I have spoken as appropriate, carry it out with firm resolve.
Having spoken thus, he then adorned that messenger with abundant jewels produced from the ocean and dispatched him toward the king.
Then those Rākṣasas, having been cursed by him, spoke in great distress: "O Lord of the Rākṣasas, grant us all liberation from this curse. (81)
Vibhīṣaṇa said: "O lowest of Rākṣasas, I shall not do so for you again."
[This is] the favor shown toward those who have made promises, and especially toward deceivers. || 82 ||
Therefore, that best of the Raghus will also show you favor; at my word, there is no doubt that some time must be awaited. (83)
Having spoken thus, the lord of the Rākṣasas then quickly dispatched a human messenger to King Kuśa, one who was a worshiper of the gods.
"Go and speak quickly to King Kuśa on my behalf: 'O Lord, show favor to these evil-minded Rākṣasas who have been cursed by me; indeed, provide for the food of these wretched ones. (85)
O best of the twice-born, having been addressed thus by him, Kuśa then departed in haste accompanied by that messenger.
Then, having gone quickly, the messenger spoke respectfully to Kuśa; bowing down according to custom, he stood there humbled by modesty. (87)
O Lord, I saw Vibhīṣaṇa at the divine Rāmeśvara; he had come there for the purpose of worship, surrounded by many Rākṣasas. (88)
"O descendant of Raghu, your entire speech has been recounted by me; and he too, bowing with humility, has heard it all. (89)
O Lord, while he was unaware, his subjects on earth were thus tormented by the most wicked-minded rākṣasas who were greedy for human flesh.

Having heard that from my mouth, he brought about the restraint of all those who had committed slaughter upon the earth, O best of kings; they were all made into *vyantara* spirits, living on sinful food and conduct. (91)
"You shall likewise become tormented by hunger and thirst. Having been thus entreated by all of them, he too, having bowed down to him again and again— 92.
"All of us have been cursed; therefore, O Lord, show us favor. Then they were addressed by him: "O lowest of Rākṣasas, I [cannot help] you. (93)
"I shall show you favor, yet I will not give you food; by my command, all of you shall be possessed of sin. (94)
Once they have been subdued, he will bestow his favor upon you; for that purpose, O lord of the earth, a messenger has been sent to your presence. (95)

Practice everything that was said by that Rākṣasa as the absolute truth; or rather, what is the use of speaking much to you? There is no devotee such as Vibhīṣaṇa, who is endowed with both devotion and power, like him.
"From this day forward, the Rākṣasas shall no longer roam upon our earth; by his word, O King, you shall undoubtedly become a partaker of happiness. (97)
O King, for the sake of the Liṅgas, that Rākṣasa made this request: "O Indra among kings, I must not come here by any means; by the word of Lord Rāma, I have no access to Jambudvīpa. (98)
Whatever task must be performed while staying here, whether it be divine or human, I shall carry out your command, even if it should be extremely difficult to accomplish.
Therefore, O Great King, that man who was sent as a messenger by the worshipper of Rāmeśvara—behold him, O Lord of the Earth! (100)
Then, accompanied by various offerings to be presented according to his instructions, that messenger, dispatched by the Lord of the Rakshasas, arrived.
Thirteen prasthas of pearls, each the size of an āmalaka fruit, were brought by him for the sake of that lord of the earth. 102.
O best of the twice-born, sixteen perfectly pure *droṇas* of beryl, emeralds, and precious gems of noble birth were brought together. (103)
There were garments purified by fire as well as those made of divine materials; indeed, there were innumerable pieces of gold, noble and beyond counting.
O twice-born ones, having shown all of that to the great-souled Kuśa and having circumambulated him, he then offered his salutation.
O tiger among kings, this Vibhīṣaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, offers his salutation with devotion; he has spoken these words through my mouth: [106]
"O Lord of the Earth, by the grace of your father, there is safety for me in your kingdom; here I remain forever, worshipping Hara on behalf of your father. (107)
O King, if anything improper has been done on the surface of the earth by those wicked-souled ones who were unknown to me, may that be forgiven of me. (108)
"O Lord, these Rākṣasas who have been cursed by me for your sake—declare what shall be the food for these who have taken the form of ghosts."
Kuśa said: "Having come here at my command, let them diligently fill all these lingas in their entirety with dust from every direction."
Therefore, O worshiper of the gods, listen attentively as I describe what their food shall be upon this earth. (111)
When the sun has entered Libra, they should come to the surface of the earth and exert themselves diligently to roam there until the appearance of Scorpio.
In that regard, those lowest of men who have not performed the *śrāddha* during the fortnight of the departed (*pretapakṣa*), or while the sun remains in Virgo until it reaches Libra; || 113 ||
By my command, the night-stalkers shall undoubtedly consume various kinds of food for one month, while remaining in their bodies in the form of fever. (114)
Those men by whom [a rite] is given devoid of rules, or consumed without following the prescribed method—even if it be a *śrāddha*—must always be served by those in the form of fevers. (115)
"In this manner, you must address all those pretas with my entire message; therefore, having come here, let them carry out my word during the month of Kārttika. (116)
Likewise, O messenger, you must say to Vibhīṣaṇa these words of mine: "Whatever harsh speech I addressed to you out of negligence, [forgive that]. (117)
"I know, O illustrious one, that there is no agitation in you at all; these words were spoken by me upon seeing people in distress. (118)
While you, the lord of the Rākṣasas, remain on the ground, I know that my father Janaka always remains with Rāma, the best among those who bear weapons.
Having spoken thus, Rāghava then honored the messenger with various kinds of garments, jewels, and diverse items produced from the rivers.
After Vibhīṣaṇa had performed his duties, Rāghava subsequently dispatched many gifts that were indeed available there.
Sūta said: Having thus made all those best of the twice-born endowed with happiness, the king afterwards gave them all these things, such as pearls and the like.
Likewise, various kinds of tribute arrived from Laṅkā, as well as other royal edicts accompanied by elephants and horses.
Various ports, villages, and cities, as well as whatever else was desired by whomsoever, were indeed given by him to that person.
Then, having established the deity Kuśeśvara and Laveśvara, those two illustrious brothers, the best of the Raghus, cast off their own bodies.
Having presented [the gifts] to the foremost of Brahmins and having provided them with their proper livelihoods, the two who had accomplished their purpose departed swiftly for the city of Ayodhyā.
Sūta said: Then, O best of the twice-born, when the lord of the day had reached the sign of Libra, the ghosts indeed filled the ground arising from the Liṅga.
Whatever was situated there—the primordial sacred ford and the abode of the gods—all that was completely filled with dust by those *vyantara* spirits.
Then, O best of the twice-born, security was established in that field, even for other worlds, as those lingas had been brought to destruction.
Then, after some time, during the course of a certain yuga, the lord of the earth, Bṛhadaśva, arrived from the Śālva country.
O best of the twice-born, having seen that vast land devoid of palaces, he set his mind upon building palaces on that site.
And having summoned many artisans there by the thousands, he had that ground, which was extensive below, cleared out.
As the earth was being dug up, numerous lingas with four faces emerged and came within the range of vision.
Then, seeing the earth covered with those lingas, that king, together with his artisans, met his death at that very moment.
From that time forward, out of fear, no mortal on this earth has built a palace, a pond, or even a well there.

Thus ends the one hundred and fifth chapter, titled "The Severing of the Rākṣasa Liṅga," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth section of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. 105.
The sages said: "Tell us which holy fords (tīrthas) and lingas were lost when the surface of the earth was completely filled with dust by those ghosts."
Sūta said: O twice-born ones, the tīrthas and liṅgas are innumerable; those that have fallen into ruin I shall describe according to their importance—be enlightened! (2)
There, the sacred ford that had disappeared is remembered as Cakratīrtha, where in ancient times the discus was placed by the powerful Viṣṇu.
Likewise, there is another sacred site of the Mothers (Mātṛtīrtha) which grants all desires to men, where those divine Mothers were established by Kārttikeya.
O Brahmins, there is likewise another excellent liṅga of the royal sage Mucukunda; however, that of King Sagara has disappeared from that place.
Of Ikṣvāku, Vasuṣeṇa, and the high-souled Kakutstha; of Aila Candradeva and the wise Kāśirāja. || 6 ||
The hermitages of Agniveśa, Raibhya, Cyavana, Bhṛgu, and likewise of Yājñavalkya, all fell into ruin there.
And of the great seer Hārīta, and of the high-souled Haryaśva, of Kutsa, Vasiṣṭha, Nārada, and Trita. || 8 ||
In that very place, there are numerous liṅgas of the wives of the sages, as well as those of Kātyāyanī, Śāṇḍilī, and Maitreyī from ancient times.
Another marvel occurred there as the surface of the earth was being filled by other wives of sages whose number is unknown. (10)
O best of Brahmins, I shall relate to you those Rākṣasas, Pāṃsus, and Pretas; this should be heard by you with well-composed minds.
Seeing the rain of dust released by the pretas on all sides, a powerful wind was then unleashed by that group of Mothers.
By him, the rain made of dust was churned away on all sides outside; it fell upon that ground, yet nothing at all remained there to fill it.
Then those Vyaṃtaras, dejected and hopeless of fulfilling his vow, went before King Kuśa and cried out to him.
O Lord of the Earth, the shower of dust created there by us is carried away in a hundred directions elsewhere by the wind released from Mātṛ.
Therefore, O King, devise a means for their destruction, by which we may fill that ground with dust on all sides.
O excellent brahmins, having heard those words of theirs, King Kuśa then reached that sacred field and propitiated Rudra.
Then, at the end of the year, the Blessed Lord Hara, having become pleased with him, said: "Pray for whatever is desired in your heart."

Kuśa said: "Just as the circle of the earth is quickly filled with dust, so do you, by your grace, act in such a way that it is likewise filled with those released from this state of being a ghost. (19)
I have already declared that it is impossible for the hosts of pretas to fulfill that [vow]; moreover, since it is being guarded by his mother, it is not possible to fulfill it.
In that place, O Lord, there are lingas established by means of mantras born of the Rākṣasas; from touching or seeing them, the destruction of people occurs.
"O Lord, because these lingas are immovable and out of fear of the sacred scriptures, we shall by no means perform any other act such as uprooting them. (22)
Therefore, O best of gods, let such a policy be enacted so that there shall be no destruction of these ascetic Brāhmaṇas caused by their physical forms.
Then the Blessed Lord Rudra, having summoned those Mothers, said: "O ladies, let this place where you are stationed be abandoned."
There, at the command of Kuśa, the pretas, remaining unperturbed by the dust, will bring about rain day and night for the welfare of the world.
The mothers said: "O Bull-bannered Lord, at your command we shall abandon that place; however, show us some other such [place] as well. (26)
"We shall dwell in this very field because of Skanda; we have been established here by him, and therefore it was said that we must remain forever. (27)
Then the Blessed One spoke from that place: "I shall grant a most excellent station for all of you individually, which shall bring auspiciousness."
O highly fortunate one, there are sixty-eight of my sacred fields situated all around, in which I am eternally present.
"Having become sixty-eight in separate divisions, you shall all abide within them by my command and receive the highest worship."
Having heard those words of the god, those mothers were then delighted and abandoned that place established by Skanda.
Having divided herself into sixty-eight parts with various distinct forms, she remains eternally established within those sixty-eight fields.
Then that entire circle of the earth, abandoned by them, was filled with dust by the hungry ghosts (pretas) who were untiring day and night. || 33 ||
O twice-born ones, having thus granted him the boon, the Blessed One whose vehicle is the bull subsequently vanished from sight along with his host of gods.
Praised by all the brahmins and ascetics from every quarter, and having received their blessings, he departed from there toward the city of Ayodhyā.

Thus ends the one hundred and sixth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Majesty of Luptatīrtha," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. 106.

The sages said: "O son of Sūta, regarding these sixty-eight sacred sites of the God of gods that have been mentioned by you, how are they situated there? Explain all of this to us, for our curiosity is indeed great."
Sūta said: This burden of questions which has been proclaimed by you is indeed great; nevertheless, having paid homage to the wielder of the Pināka bow, I shall recount it.
Formerly, in the city of Camatkārapura, there lived an excellent Brāhmaṇa named Citraśarman, of great renown, born in the lineage of Vatsa.
This thought arose in him: "I shall bring Hāṭakeśvara from Pātāla here and worship him with devotion day and night. (4)
Having thus made this resolution, he thereafter practiced austerity, self-restrained, restricted in diet, and established in the highest steadfastness.
O best of Brahmins, after a long time, the Blessed Lord Śambhu was pleased with him and then spoke to him respectfully.
"Choose a boon, O best of Brahmins, whatever dwells in your mind; even the sovereignty of the three worlds I shall grant to you without doubt, for I am pleased. (7)
Therefore, constantly pray for that which is established in your mind, which is difficult to attain even for all the gods, and especially for human beings.
Citraśarman said: "O God, if you are pleased with me and if you grant me a boon, then come here from Pātāla in the form of a Liṅga, O Lord of the Gods."
May that Liṅga known as Hāṭakeśvara, which is established by Brahmā and situated in Pātāla, truly come here quickly.
The Blessed Lord said: O best of the twice-born, every linga everywhere is indeed immovable; how much more so that first one which was fashioned by Brahmā himself?
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, install that linga made of hāṭaka; it shall become famous in the world by the name Hāṭakeśvara.
On a Monday coinciding with the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, that man who, endowed with faith and possessed of devotion to Him, shall perform worship; || 3 ||
"O twice-born one, through worship you shall obtain the supreme good arising from the primordial Liṅga. Having spoken thus, the Blessed One then vanished from sight.
Then Citraśarman, having constructed a most beautiful palace, devoutly installed a golden Liṅga there.
And he performed worship there daily according to the procedure prescribed in the scriptures; consequently, O twice-born ones, that liṅga became famous throughout the three worlds.
People come from afar and worship him thereafter; furthermore, whatever other more virtuous twice-born ones were stationed there, [they too honored him]. (17)
Then, upon seeing his extraordinary feat, a rivalry arose among all of them, who were born from the same place and were equally endowed with excellent qualities. (18)

"Although he is devoid of merit, he is renowned throughout the three worlds because he has attained the propitiation of Hara; therefore, we shall please Hara for his sake, so that equality may be produced. (19)
Sixty-eight sacred sites of the Trident-bearer are recorded in the world, where the Supreme Lord manifests his presence during the three periods of the day. (20)
And sixty-eight clans of ours are established here; with this deluded mind, they share common characteristics. (22)
Therefore, having propitiated the three-eyed Lord, he brought here that very *liṅga* which was situated in the netherworld (*pātāla*). || 22 ||
Likewise, all of you must worship Maheśvara through the power of your asceticism and bring back all the sacred emblems of the fields in their entirety.
Śaṅkara will bring about the welfare of all these lineages—whatever lineage is connected with the sacred field, and whatever else there may be.
Then all those best of the twice-born, endowed with peace, performed ascetic practices that were difficult for all living beings to accomplish.
By means of recitations, fire-oblations, fasts, and various kinds of observances, as well as by offerings, worship, gifts, ablutions, and charities; (26)
Having installed the Liṅga of the God, renowned by the name Dvijeśvara, in a most beautiful, lofty temple resembling a mountain.
Having abandoned all domestic activities as well as those arising from sacrifices and other worldly pursuits, they satisfy Maheśvara.
O twice-born ones, even though he was being propitiated in this manner, the Supreme Lord did not attain satisfaction, nor did he reach the highest state of contentment by any means whatsoever.
Then, at the end of a thousand years, having propitiated Maheśvara, they did not obtain any fruit whatsoever; thereupon, they all became enraged.
O Śūlin, even for this most foolish Citraśarman, you have attained supreme satisfaction in a very short time.
We have reached old age, and though we have worshipped Śaṅkara since childhood, we have not seen you, O Supreme Lord. (32)
Therefore, everyone must enter the fire; for this is the resolution we have now made in your presence.
Then, having gathered wood, all those best of the twice-born, meditating upon the Lord in their minds, constructed various kinds of funeral pyres.
Likewise, having performed all the ritual procedures, including bathing, giving gifts, and so forth, all those brahmins [approached] the well-kindled sacrificial fire.
As many times as they entered together with their sons, being composed in meditation, so many times did the Blessed One, being pleased, go to meet them.
And laughing aloud, he spoke with a voice as deep as a thundercloud, as if restoring all those best of Brahmins to life: || 37 ||
"O tigers among Brahmins, do not, do not commit such a great act of rashness! Do this at my word, especially since I am already satisfied. (38)
Therefore, speak that which is established in your minds, so that by giving it, I may return once more to my own world. (39)
The Brahmins said: "O best of gods, in this sacred field and in the vicinity of this city, there are sixty-eight fields which are celebrated by people as auspicious. (40)
O best of gods, let him always come together with those primordial *liṅgas*, so that our indignation here may be pacified for all of us. (41)
"This man, devoid of all virtues, vies with us all; therefore, perform this [remedy] through the power of your linga. (42)
Sūta said: In the meantime, the brahmin Citraśarman, perceiving that Hara was the granter of boons, spoke to Maheśvara while filled with rivalry. (43)
Citraśarman said: "O Lord of Gods, by these acts beginning with the renunciation of your life, and thereafter by performing very great penance, you have been brought to satisfaction."
"O Lord of the Gods, because we were competing with him and were merely proud of our own virtues, nothing at all should be given by you to him. (46)
If you disregard me and bestow your desired [gift] upon them, along with these sons and wife, in your very presence, I shall enter the fire; therefore, act appropriately.
Sūta said: Having heard those words of his, the Lord whose crest is the moon reflected in his mind, "What would be the meritorious deed to be done here? (47)
These tigers among Brahmins will meet their destruction on my account; even this best of the twice-born, who is fully accomplished and equal to a Gaṇa. (48)
Therefore, I must act through both means so that there may be happiness in this field, especially for the brahmins and likewise for those who dwell here. (49)
This very task has always been present in my mind as well: "I shall indeed place all my buddha-fields within a single location. (50)
Likewise, there will come a terrible time arising from the Kali age; during that period, the sacred fields and holy fords on the surface of the earth will go to destruction.
Out of fear of him, all the holy fords have taken refuge in this sacred field; I too shall bring all my own sacred fields here in their entirety.
Then Maheśvara spoke this to Citraśarman: "Listen to my entire speech, and carry it out immediately thereafter. (53)
"O best of the twice-born, let all my fields here come together, and let the Brahmins arrive and rejoice. (54)
"I shall also bring about your supreme fitness, O high-minded one, if you abide by my word, casting aside the rivalry born of your twice-born status. (55)
Your fourth lineage as well shall be proclaimed by all those twice-born ones according to the sequence declared in the Vedas, and they shall also proclaim your primacy.
Likewise, O twice-born one, I shall bestow upon you another honor as well, which shall endure as long as the moon and sun, and which includes undoubtedly sons, grandsons, and so forth. (57)
In your lineage, sons, grandsons, and others likewise shall arise when the śrāddha rite or the libation (tarpaṇa) is performed according to the prescribed injunctions. (58)
Having first uttered the name of the one known as Vatsa, together with his lineage, they shall likewise proclaim his names out of devotion.
Then they shall satisfy the ancestors and grandfathers, as well as other kinsmen, friends, relatives, and blood relations.
Those who, being deluded, offer libations to the ancestors in your lineage without using your name, their [act] will be in vain. (61)
Whether it be a śrāddha rite, a gift, or an offering of libations, they all originate from you; therefore, abandoning egoism, worship me alone. 62.
"By which you, though already perfected, shall attain supreme and eternal perfection. Having thus instructed that Brahmin, he made him both the first and the last.

Then he said to those Brahmins, "Let a temple be built. O twice-born ones, an unsurpassed Liṅga should be installed for each respective lineage (gotra), so that my transition [into them] may take place within them."
Then those brahmins, having repeatedly beheld the charming plots of land there, built palaces filled with joy. || 65 ||

They installed sixty-eight divine lingas of various kinds, resembling the peaks of Mount Kailāsa; and they gave each of them the name corresponding to the specific sacred field (kṣetra) in which it was situated.

Then, after some time had passed, the three-eyed god, having come again into their sight, spoke these sweet words, having been propitiated by the power of their asceticism following the installation of the Liṅga.
The Blessed Lord said: "O best of Brahmins, I am truly well-pleased with you today; therefore, this entire task of mine has been accomplished by you."
Therefore, out of fear of the Kali age, our lingas and sacred fields shall be honored by you alone; this will not be possible through others.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, quickly pray for stability of mind; I shall grant it swiftly, even if it be very difficult to attain. (70)
The Brāhmaṇas said: "O Lord, O Sovereign of the Gods, if you are pleased with us, then let Citraśarman be made by you today just as the first one was. (71)
"Without doubt, our name should always be proclaimed in all śrāddha rites, so that by your grace we may now become equal to Citraśarman. (72)
The Blessed Lord said: "Even among you, whatever men shall come under [their] influence—whether they be youths, endowed with the scriptures, or experts in Vedic knowledge—" (73)
"You shall bring those known as the *āmuṣyāyaṇas*; they will remain eternally in that field, making the offerings of the *śrāddha* inexhaustible. (74)
Having spoken thus, the Lord of Gods then vanished from sight; those Brahmins, being well-satisfied, remained established in that place.
Thus, O best of Brahmins, all the sacred fields and shrines there always dwell, for they are afraid of the Kali age.
Thus, having attained perfection through the worship of the Lord, those brahmins became renowned throughout the entire world as performers of inexhaustible śrāddha rites.

Thus ends the one hundred and seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Account of the Installation of the Liṅga by the Brāhmaṇa Citraśarman," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. 107.
The sages said: O son of Sūta, please proclaim to us by name those sixty-eight sacred fields that have been mentioned by you.
Likewise, proclaim in their entirety those other holy places that exist upon the surface of the earth; for our curiosity is indeed great.
Sūta said: O best of the twice-born, those sixty-eight sacred fords (tīrthas) and likewise the sacred fields (kṣetras) upon the earth that have been mentioned by you—
O tigers among sages, all those sacred fords, being terrified by sin in this Kali age, have entered the subterranean realm (rasātala).
O twice-born ones, this very matter which you have asked me regarding the pilgrimage was previously asked of the Supreme Lord by Pārvatī.
In ancient times, the Lord Maheśvara was seated upon the peak of Kailāsa, sitting on an excellent throne together with all the hosts of his attendants.

When the immortals had arrived for the purpose of offering salutations and had all departed for their celestial abode, O best of Brahmins, the Goddess, seated upon half of his throne, spoke these words.
The Goddess said: O God of gods, O Mahādeva, whose crest is washed by the Gaṅgā, tell me the majesty of the sacred fords (tīrtha) if I am dear to you.
"O Lord, there are three and a half crores of sacred fords here on this earth; please recount them to me now by their names and their number."

O Lord, O Ruler of the Gods, please recount those many sacred fords (tīrthas) and holy fields belonging to me, which are easily accessible for embodied beings; for by the recitation of all these sacred fords, their full fruit is obtained.
Īśvara said: O lady of beautiful hips, the word "tīrtha" is used in the context of religious duties. Listen with a concentrated mind to the truth regarding all places of dharma. 11.

The mother is a sacred ford, the father is a sacred ford, and the company of the virtuous is a sacred ford; likewise, reflection upon dharma, as well as restraint and self-discipline, are sacred fords.
O lady of beautiful hips, meritorious discourses have been composed by the divine sages; likewise, O beloved, they are the refuge of the great lords of holy men and of the gods.

These regions of the earth shall be pure and are indeed proclaimed as sacred fords (tīrthas). Merely by seeing them, remembering them, or bathing in them, living beings are liberated from sins even those accumulated over hundreds of births. (14)
Likewise, those who are sinners and those who are betrayers of trust—all of them are liberated in that same way by immersing themselves in it.

In this way, O lady beautiful in every limb, all sins go to destruction; even the sin that arises for embodied beings here from the killing of a Brahmin, that too undoubtedly reaches its dissolution through contact with a sacred ford (tīrtha). || 16 ||
In former times, the skull that was attached to my hand also fell due to contact with those sacred fords and by bathing in them.
Thus, at all sacred fords as well as in holy shrines, one should bathe with a mind endowed with devotion and directed toward no other object.
O large-eyed one, by bathing properly where my abode—which destroys all sins and especially grants the desires of both men and women—is located, the fruit of all [meritorious acts] is obtained. (19)
O Goddess, this most secret [teaching] is eternally established within me; it has not been told by me to anyone, not even to the Lord of the Gods (Indra) when he questioned me.
"O blessed one, O fair-faced lady, because of my affection for you, I have indeed told you that sixty-eight holy places (tīrthas) are to be visited with devotion by human beings. (21)
Those very shrines of mine are the removers of all sins and the granters of desires, O lady of beautiful hips; this is undoubtedly due to my power. (22)
Whatever desire a man may have set his heart upon, if he performs his bath at that sacred ford and then worships the god Maheśvara, [that desire shall be fulfilled].

O lady of excellent hips, let alone the sight or the touch of those men by whom Hari has been worshipped after meditating upon his virtuous deeds in their minds; even by mere remembrance, men are liberated from the sins committed in the past. (24)
O beautiful one, these gods, Śakra and the others, as well as Nārada and others, having worshipped me at those sacred fords, attained the third heaven. (25)
I shall declare them to you in detail, one by one; listen to their names, O Goddess of gods, remaining with a concentrated mind. (26)
Vārāṇasī, Prayāga, and likewise Naimiṣa; the highly meritorious Gayāśiras and the pure Kurujāṅgala. (27)
Prabhāsa, Puṣkara, and another, Viśveśvara; Aṭṭahāsa, Mahendra, and likewise that which is Ujjayanī.
Marukoṭi, Śaṅkukarṇa, and Gokarṇa, the most excellent sacred field; Rudrakoṭi, Sthaleśa, Harṣita, and Vṛṣabhadhvaja. (29)
Likewise, the field of Kedāra, the field of Madhyamakeśvara, the field of Sahasrākṣa, and another, Kārtikeśvara.
In the same way, Vastramārga is remembered, as well as Kanakhala; and Bhadrakarṇa is renowned, and likewise that which is called Daṇḍaka.
Likewise, there is the sacred field known as Tridaṇḍa, as well as Kṛmijāṅgala; the sacred field Ekāmra, and likewise the sacred field Chāgalaka. || 32 ||
O Goddess of the gods, [he visited] Kāliñjara, as well as another Maṇḍaleśvara, Kāśmīra, Marukeśa, and the very beautiful Hariścandra.
Puraścandra, Vāmeśa, Kukuṭeśvara, Bhasmagātra, Oṃkāra, Trisaṃdhyā, and likewise Virajā.
Arkeśvara, Nepāla, Duṣkarṇa, Karavīraka, Jāgeśvara, and likewise, O Goddess, Śrīśaila, the best of mountains. (35)
Ayodhyā, Pātāla, and the great Kārohaṇa; the holy river Devikā, and Bhairava at the eastern ocean.
Likewise, the Saptagodāvarī-tīrtha is proclaimed, as well as Nirmaleśa and the very beautiful Karṇikāra. (37)
Kailāsa, the banks of the Jāhnavī, the Jalaliṅga, the Vāḍava fire, the excellent Badarītīrtha, and likewise Koṭitīrtha.
Vindhya Mountain, Hemakūṭa, and Gandhamādana; likewise Liṅgeśvara, the sacred field (kṣetra), and Laṅkādvāra as well. || 39 ||
Naleśvara, Madhyeśa, Kedāra, Rudrajālaka, the one named Suvarṇa, Vāmoru, and another, Ṣaṣṭikāpatha—[these are the sixty]. (40)

Thus ends the one hundred and eighth chapter, titled "Description of the Sixty-Eighth Tīrtha," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 108 ||
Īśvara said: O fair-faced one, all this that I was asked by you has been told to you—the essence of all holy places (tīrthas), the compendium of tīrthas. || 1 ||
O lady of excellent hips, I am established in all of these very places; and for the sake of the welfare of the gods, I exist under other names in other sacred sites as well. (2)
That man who, having bathed in these sacred fords, beholds me and proclaims my name through its recitation, shall surely attain liberation. || 3 ||
The illustrious Goddess said: "O Lord, tell me in its entirety those names which are to be proclaimed by you at various holy places (tīrthas), since I am your beloved."
Īśvara said: One should worship Mahādeva at Vārāṇasī, Maheśvara at Prayāga, Devadeva at Naimiṣa, and Prapitāmaha at Gayā. || 5 ||
They know Sthāṇu to be at Kurukṣetra, Śaśiśekhara at Prabhāsa, Ajāgandhi at Puṣkara, and likewise Viśva at Viśveśvara.
At Aṭṭahāsa he is Mahānāda; at Mahendra, Mahāvratam; at Ujjayinī, Mahākāla; and at Marukoṭa, Mahotkaṭa. || 7 ||
One of great splendor at Śaṅkukarṇa, one of great strength at Gokarṇa, one of great yoga at Rudrakoṭi, and the Mahāliṅga at Sthaleśvara.
Likewise, he worshipped Harṣa at Harṣita, Vṛṣabha at Vṛṣabhadhvaja, Īśāna at Kedāra, and Śarva at Madhyamakeśvara.
O Goddess, one should worship Suparṇākṣa at Sahasrākṣa, Susūkṣma at Kārtikeśvara, Bhava at Vastrāpatha, and likewise Ugra at Kanakhala.
One should worship Bhadrakarṇa at Śiva, Daṇḍin at Daṇḍaka, Ūrdhvaretas at Tridaṇḍā, and Caṇḍīśa at Kṛmijāṅgala.
Likewise, one should worship Kṛttivāsa at Ekāmra, Kapardin at Chāgaleya, Nīlakaṇṭha at Kāliñjara, and Śrīkaṇṭha at Maṇḍaleśvara.
Vijaya in Kāśmīra, Jayanta in Marukeśvara, Hara in Hariścandra, and Śaṅkara in Puraścandra. || 13 ||
One should know Jaṭī at Vāmeśvara, Saumya at Kukkuṭeśvara, Bhūteśvara at Bhasmagātra, and Amarakaṇṭaka at Oṃkāra.
Tryambaka is to be known at Trisandhyā, Trilocana at Virajā, Dīpta at Arkeśvara, and Paśupālaka in Nepāla. || 15 ||
Yamaliṅga is at Duṣkarṇa, Kapālī is at Karavīraka, Triśūlī is at Jāgeśvara, and Tripurāntaka is at Śrīśaila.
Rohaṇa is in Ayodhyā, Hāṭakeśvara is in Pātāla, Nakulīśa is in Kārohaṇa, and Umāpati is in Devikā.
In Bhairava, he is the immortal one in the form of Bhairava; in the Eastern Ocean, he is Bhīma; at Saptagodāvara, he is Svayaṃbhū; and at Nirmaleśvara, [he is] Svayaṃbhū.
One should worship Gaṇādhyakṣa at Karṇikāra, Gaṇādhipa at Kailāsa, Himasthāna at Gaṅgādvāra, and Jalapriya at Jaliṅga.
Anala at Vāḍava-agni, Bhīma at Badarikāśrama, Śreṣṭha at Koṭīśvara, and Vārāha on the Vindhya mountain. (20)
Virūpākṣa on Hemakūṭa, Bhūrbhuva on Gandhamādana, Varada at Liṅgeśvara, and Narāntaka in Laṅkā.
O Goddess, these sixty-eight [names] have been specifically recounted to you; they destroy all sins for those who recite or even hear them.
Therefore, with every effort, it should be recited by the wise at all three times of the day; especially so by those who are pure and have been initiated into the Śiva-dīkṣā.
O lady of excellent hips, even if this [mantra] is merely written down, wherever it remains in a house, no evil arising from spirits or ghosts shall occur there. (24)
Neither from disease, nor from serpents, nor from thieves, O fair-faced one, nor from others such as kings and the like, shall there ever be any danger anywhere at any time. (25)
The Goddess said: O best of gods, among all these places on earth, human beings—even those who have attained long lifespans—are in no way able to bathe there. (1)
Proclaim to me the most essential among these sacred fords (tīrthas), by bathing in which a man properly obtains the fruit of them all.
Īśvara said: O Goddess, among these there is an unsurpassed group of eight holy fords (tīrthas); by bathing there, men obtain the fruit of all [the aforementioned rites]. || 3 ||
Naimiṣa, Kedāra, Puṣkara, Kṛmijāṅgala, Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, Prabhāsa, and Hāṭakeśvara. || 4 ||
Whoever bathes in these eight, endowed with perfect faith, has bathed in all sacred fords; this which I have spoken is the truth.
The Goddess said: O Mahādeva, how will it be possible in the Kali age? Therefore, tell me of my bath, which is indeed the very essence of all sacred fords (tīrtha).
O God of gods, O Three-eyed One, if I am dear to you, devoted, and likewise compliant with your will, [then grant this] for all eight of these as well.
Īśvara said: O Goddess of the gods, among all eight sacred fields there is one that is supreme; even among those, the field known as Hāṭakeśvara is the most excellent.
Where all my sacred fields are established by my command, as well as other holy fords (tīrthas), even while the Kali age persists.
Therefore, that sacred field must indeed be resorted to with every effort by humans desiring liberation; this which I have spoken is the truth. (10)
Sūta said: O best of the twice-born, I have thus related to you this entire collection arising from the sixty-eight [tīrthas], accompanied by their names and deities.
Just as it was declared by the gracious Lord regarding the supreme secret of Pārvatī, so has it been related by me in its entirety to you all.
Whoever recites this with devotion, which originates from the sixty-eight [sacred sites], obtains the merit born of bathing; likewise, one who hears it endowed with faith [obtains the same]. (13)

Thus ends the one hundred and tenth chapter, titled "Description of the Majesty of the Sixty-eighth Tīrtha," in the Śrī-Hāṭakeśvara-Kṣetra-Māhātmya of the Nāgara-Khaṇḍa, within the sixth section of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. 110.
The sages said: O son of Sūta, tell us in detail all the lineages (gotras) of those brahmins by whom the sacred sites of Śiva were brought there.
When that time had arrived, by whose grace were the brahmins born of such lineages able to acquire sacred fields through the favor of Śaṅkara? (2)
O son of Sūta, how many lineages were established by that devoted Anarta in that most excellent city of Camatkārapura?
"You previously declared that a city was given to the twice-born after having constructed it; yet their number was not specified. Therefore, please proclaim that."

Sūta said: Formerly, an instruction was given by seventy-two lords of sages. In the past, the sovereign of Ānarta, afflicted by the disease of leprosy, arrived at Śaṅkha-tīrtha and performed his ablutions with great haste.
By that [act], at that very moment, the leprosy of that king vanished due to the majesty of that sacred ford (tīrtha), as he had become despondent regarding his body.
Then, having become free from disease and filled with great joy, he prostrated himself again and again before those best of sages and spoke to them.
"I shall bestow upon you gold, or elephants and horses, or even the entire kingdom; therefore, speak, O best of the twice-born."
O twice-born ones, whatever else may please him, however much it may be—let favor be shown to me, who am wretched and prostrate before you. (9)
The Brahmins said: "O twice-born ones, we are forest-dwellers whose dharma is non-possessiveness; we wash [our feet] immediately after eating. What use have we for a kingdom or for wealth? (10)
The king said:
He who, having received a benefit, does not return it with a good deed, but instead commits evil against that benefactor, is declared to be ungrateful. || 11 ||
For the slayer of a Brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, the breaker of trust, and the rogue, atonement has been prescribed by the virtuous; but for the ungrateful, there is no atonement.
Therefore, O best of the twice-born, show me favor and say something, by which I may attain freedom from my debt, even if it should mean a life of hardship.
The sages said: "O highly fortunate one, this is true: there is no atonement for an ungrateful person. However, in that case, fault would lie with the giver if he were full of desire."
O Indra among kings, where one who is free from desire acts for the sake of another's benefit, not even the slightest fault arises there in any way whatsoever.
Therefore, go and protect your own kingdom according to your own duty, by which happiness is produced both in this world and in the next. (16)
Thus forbidden in a thousand ways by the brahmins, that lord of the earth, with great difficulty, bowed deeply to them and then departed for his own home.

Having gone there, having made himself joyful and having fashioned a beautiful image of Maheśvara, he ruled his kingdom as before—its thorns entirely destroyed—with songs, dances, instrumental music, and night vigils.
Day and night he constantly reflected regarding those brahmins: "How shall I be of service to these best of the twice-born, by whom this new body of mine was given back to me? (19)
All those best of sages, endowed with the power of moving through the sky, travel to various sacred fords out of devotion by the power of their asceticism.
Having performed their ablutions, recitations, and likewise the libations for the ancestors in those waters, they returned to their own hermitage and resumed their sustenance.
Some twice-born ones perform their daily rites right there, while others, having reached the distant and enchanting holy site, behold it.
Having stayed there for one night or even two nights, others returned home; yet others arrived after three nights had passed. || 23 ||
Neither in Vārāṇasī, nor at Prayāga, nor at Puṣkara, nor at Naimiṣa; nor at Prabhāsa, nor at Kedāra, nor indeed in any other place is it so desired. (24)
Then once, on the full moon day of Kārttika at the three Puṣkara lakes, all those best of the twice-born went there, having made a firm resolve for the purpose of bathing.
"We shall dwell there for five nights with concentrated minds; therefore, you must protect our wives according to your ability. (26)
When those best of the twice-born had thus made their agreement and departed, the husband perceived that no one remained there.
Among those lords of sages dwelling in the hermitages of excellent holy sites, there was one renowned as Damayantī, whose face was like the orb of the moon.
He spoke to her thus in private: "O lady of beautiful smiles, go now; this is certainly my command regarding the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara."
"Give whatever ornaments they desire to those wives of the sages of purified souls who reside there. (30)
O lady of beautiful hips, their husbands do not accept anything from us under any circumstances, even though they are tempted by us in many ways. (31)
The anxiety born of ornaments is always greater for women; likewise, fickleness and curiosity regarding ornaments are ever-present. (32)
A woman may wear an ornament made of clay, or perhaps one made of wood and thread, or even one made of lacquer or glass. (33)
O lotus-petal-eyed one, this alone is the possible way for them to be of service; there is no other means whatsoever. (34)
Having agreed, saying "So be it," and taking various ornaments, she, filled with joy, then went to that sacred field.
There were also beautiful earrings made of jewels and pearls, as well as necklaces radiant as the moon and large anklets.
And they were inlaid with sapphire, emerald, and beryl, as well as with ruby, diamond, and beautiful māṇikya gems. (37)
With hair adorned by divine and auspicious bracelets resembling Indra’s bow, and likewise with golden threads and excellent girdles; || 38 ||
Then, when the auspicious day for the awakening of Viṣṇu had arrived, she, devoted to fasting, bathed in a certain body of water.
Having established that mountain of great ornaments upon the shore, its fierce radiance pervaded the entire circle of the sky.
In the meantime, the female ascetics arrived, filled with curiosity: "What is that queen like? What is her form, and what are her ornaments? (41)
Then, having beheld her—adorned with divine ornaments, possessed of beautiful limbs, and established in meditative absorption—they conceived this thought in their minds: || 42 ||
Blessed is this wife of the king, who, adorned with ornaments, is Damayantī herself—richly endowed with beauty and marked by every auspicious characteristic.
Having reached the conclusion of her meditation and beholding those female ascetics, Damayantī also paid homage to them all according to the prescribed rites.

To them, with palms joined in reverence, he spoke these charming and captivating words: "Today, having bathed and fasted on the day of Lord Hari, I have prepared this collection of ornaments intended for the one whose banner is Garuḍa."
Therefore, let the female ascetics accept these various ornaments given by me with desire; let this be an act of grace toward me.
Then one among them said: "This pearl necklace is mine; give this to me, O beloved of the king, for I have no other desire. (47)
Then, laughing loudly, she herself washed her feet and gave her a pearl necklace accompanied by divine garments; its pure pearls were each equal in weight to six māṣas.

O best of the twice-born, just as stars appear in the sky during the autumn season, so another woman, filled with rivalry, requested from him of stainless luster a supreme necklace that was priceless and a source of great delight to the heart. (49)
Then, taking him by the hand, she gave him her necklace; at that moment, another woman, longing for adornment, seized the necklace.
Then, O twice-born ones, the remaining female ascetics, eager for ornaments and full of rivalry, took those ornaments for themselves. (51)
Having fashioned another most enchanting ornament from a different mine, he then seized her by force after having overpowered her.
In whatever manner the female ascetics, adorned with ornaments, took hold of her, in that very same way joy arose in the heart of this Damayantī.
O best of the twice-born, he then hurled hundreds and thousands of other [missiles], yet even so, no satisfaction arose in them.
Then, having attained the state of being without ornaments, that beloved of the king joyfully said to them all, "Let contentment be felt."
Furthermore, I shall bring her again at dawn; of this there is no doubt. And whatever other diverse things she may desire, those too I shall provide.
Then they all said: "Go, O beloved of the king; you must come again, taking these ornaments with you. (57)
O excellent brahmins, having been addressed thus by them, the king’s beloved wife prostrated herself and, filled with joy, quickly departed toward her own city.
Then the female ascetics also went home and, full of rivalry, placed various garments and ornaments upon their bodies.
Except for the four female ascetics who remained firm in their vows, the remaining women took up the ornaments according to their desire.
Then, at the clear dawn when the orb of the sun had risen, that queen once again [donned] her ornaments and garments.
In that very manner he gave them to her, and they accepted them in the same way; thus, as she was offering them day after day with devotion, || 62 ||
Five nights have passed; those beloved wives of the ascetics are satisfied, yet the queen does not reach satiety as she offers [oblations] with great devotion.

Then the female ascetics there heard that she had four companions who were entirely free from desire; though they wore bark garments and deer skins, they did not approach her side. And no other women, having seen her adorned, felt any envy whatsoever.
Then, on the fifth day, that irreproachable woman went quickly to their side and took their highly precious ornaments.
Then he said to them all, "Let favor be shown; let these ornaments be accepted for the sake of decoration. (66)
The female ascetics said: "We have no need for ornaments; we are adorned by our bark garments. Therefore, go to your own palace and bestow [these things] upon those who seek them. (67)
O best of the twice-born, while they were conversing in this manner with her, four husbands arrived separately for each of them.
Then Śunaḥśepa, Śākreya, Bauddha, and the fourth, Dānta—these four indeed returned to their own hermitages by way of the sky. (69)

All the others, having suffered a loss of their status and resorted to the path of the earth, saw their own hermitage with its ornaments transformed into distorted forms; then they cried out, "What is this? What is this?", for the female ascetics had been mocked.
"By what evildoer has this hermitage of ours been thus mocked, after having taken away the ornaments and garments of the female ascetics? (71)
His wives said: "She who is established here as the wife of King Camatkāra—"
Indeed, all her ornaments were bestowed by her upon them all.
That beloved of the king has indeed arrived at our house today to bestow ornaments, but she was forbidden by us this very day.
Sūta said: Having heard those words of theirs, they then became overwhelmed with anger and repeatedly spoke to the king's wife, intent on pronouncing a curse upon her. (74)
Seventy-two years ago, we went to Puṣkara for the purpose of bathing on the full moon day of Kārttika, traveling through the path of the sky with the speed of mind and wind.
These four who have arrived are such that no acceptance of their wives was ever made by that king, even in any way, for the sake of a wicked wife. (76)
"Therefore, since this hermitage of ascetics is being mocked, you shall become a contemptible stone. (707)
Then, at that very moment, immediately after the words of the sage, she became motionless and turned into the form of a stone.
Then her retinue, overwhelmed by that grief, with eyes filled with tears and dejected, set out toward their own city.
O best of Brahmins, he related all that concerning the origin of Damayantī, as well as the account of her arising from a curse.
Having heard that account concerning the origin of the curse, the king then immediately went to the forest, distressed, in order to propitiate the brahmins.
Then those four sages, quickly learning that the lord of the earth had arrived for the sake of propitiating them in order to obtain a wife, [acted accordingly].
Then, taking with them their sacred fires and their wives, they quickly proceeded by way of the sky to Kurukṣetra. || 83 ||
The king, too, having searched for those sages everywhere with great effort, became despondent, afflicted by fatigue, and distressed by the calamity that had befallen his wife.
Then he went to that place where his wife, made of stone, was situated, surrounded on all sides by throngs of female ascetics. || 85 ||
Then, seeing her in such a state, surrounded by all his servants, he cried out "Alas! Alas! repeatedly and fell to the ground in a swoon.
Then, having regained consciousness with great difficulty after being sprinkled with water, he began to lament, repeatedly recalling the virtues of his beloved.
"Alas, my beloved, with eyes like those of a young fawn, you who are the destroyer of my life! O fair-faced one, having abandoned me—your dear and beloved husband—where have you gone today? (88)
While I had not eaten, you did not eat; while I was not awake, you did not go to sleep. Never, out of pride in your good fortune, have you ever transgressed my command. (89)
I do not recall you ever having spoken a harsh word, O large-eyed one, even in private—how much less so in the assembly at the meal? (90)
Sūta said: While the king was thus lamenting piteously at great length, his ministers arrived upon hearing that the monarch was in such a state.
Then, having with great difficulty awakened him by means of many extensive examples concerning the occurrence of great calamities that befell royal sages of antiquity, [he spoke]. (92)
They led away that wretched king, his eyes clouded with tears, sighing like a serpent, and utterly bereft of his former luster.

Having constructed a most beautiful dwelling all around her, he provided his wife—even though she remained in the form of a stone—with camphor, agallochum incense, and other offerings, as well as garments, saffron, and sandalwood.

Thus ends the one hundred and eleventh chapter, titled "The Narration of the Grief of the Lord of Ānarta upon Damayantī’s Transformation into Stone due to the Curse of a Brāhmaṇa," within the *Damayantī-upākhyāna* of the *Śrī-Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya*, in the sixth section (*Nāgara-khaṇḍa*) of the *Śrī-skānda Mahāpurāṇa*, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 111 ||
Sūta said: Then, after a few days had passed, when that lord of the earth had departed for his own home, afflicted with grief and accompanied by his retinue.
Indeed, sixty-eight of the best of the twice-born arrived on foot; they were exhausted, their limbs emaciated, and their faces grey with dust.
He saw his own wives adorned with divine ornaments, well-clad in celestial garments, like other wives of kings.
Then, overcome with wonder and afflicted by hunger, those sinful ones asked: "What is this? What is this? Why has such a contrary body been assumed? (4)
"How were these garments and excellent ornaments obtained? Surely a lapse in our movement occurred in the sky; it could not have happened otherwise."
Having completely abandoned this transformation, those highly censured wives of the ascetics then related the entire account concerning you.
O twice-born ones, [I shall tell] how Queen Damayantī, the beloved of the king, arrived and how she indeed bestowed ornaments upon them.

Thus was the curse incurred by the high-souled Brahmins. Then those sages, having heard that censurable speech, became enraged; for the acceptance of gifts from a king is contemptible, especially for ascetics.
Then, overcome by great anger and trembling uncontrollably, they seized water for the purpose of destroying the king and his kingdom.
By this wicked and evil king, our natural aerial power has been destroyed; he has enticed away our genuine wives and all our honest attendants, by which such a calamity as this has come to pass.
Sūta said: While those sages were thus pronouncing their curse upon that lord of the earth, his wives, filled with rage, spoke as follows.
O best of Brahmins, a curse should not be cast upon that king; rather, our words must be heard by you without hesitation. (12)
We all have been adorned by the wife of the lord of men with excellent garments and divine ornaments, with a mind purified by faith. (13)
"Due to the fault of poverty, we have always remained in your house; emaciated, we have not obtained even the happiness that arises for mortals. (14)
For those who are devoted to austerity, the world beyond exists right here; nor shall there be even the slightest fruit of mortality for them. (15)
This world is proclaimed here as the domain of others—of those base and evil-minded people whose minds are attached to worldly enjoyments. (16)
For those in the householder stage of life whose minds are devoted to their own duty, both this world and the next are attained; of this there is no doubt. || 17 ||
Therefore, we have no doubt that by following this supreme householder stage of life (gṛhasthāśrama), we shall accomplish the two unsurpassed worlds.
Therefore, those who are composed declare that houses are delightful when one has obtained land and the desired means of livelihood from a king.
And then, behold the arising of sons and grandsons, as well as the happiness of the daughters and especially of their kinsmen. (20)
If you do not carry out these words spoken by us, we shall all give up our lives; of this there is no doubt. (21)
Being thus joined with the sin of killing a woman, you will thereafter certainly go to the difficult Raurava hell. || 22 ||
Having thus heard those words of theirs, the sages indeed cast upon the surface of the earth the water held in their hands for the purpose of a curse.
Then, O best of the twice-born, that portion of the earth was scorched by that water and attained the state of a saline wasteland even today.
Let whatever grows there, such as grass and the like, not sprout; and let it not obtain birth again, whether as a bird or even as an insect. (25)
Even a blade of grass or a deer there [attains merit]; how much more so a devoted man who performs a *śrāddha* there with faith during the month of Phālguna? (26)
On the full moon day falling on a Sunday, he shall deliver his own ancestors, even those who have reached a hell of terrible form due to their own actions.

Thus ends the one hundred and twelfth chapter, titled "The Narration of the Greatness of the Origin of the Barren Soil," within the Legend of Damayantī, in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, the sixth part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. 112.

Sūta said: Thereupon, all those Brāhmaṇas, their anger having subsided, set their minds upon the performance of sacrifices, upon the life of householdership, and upon the procreation of sons and grandsons.
In the meantime, having heard that those best of the twice-born had arrived, the king, filled with devotion, approached them for the purpose of prostration.
Having heard the news that she had become enraged, as well as the words concerning her wife uttered by those who had not entered the householder’s life, which were intended to pacify her; || 3 ||
Then, having prostrated before them all with the eight limbs of his body, that lord of the earth, standing humbly with palms joined in reverence, spoke.
"Through your grace, the fruit of my birth has been attained by me through the destruction of this disease; therefore, tell me, what shall I do? (5)
The Brāhmaṇas said: O Indra among kings, by your wife—who has bestowed upon us various jewels—we who dwell everywhere have been rendered fulfilled.
Therefore, having established an excellent city right here in this most beautiful field, grant us the state of householdership, so that offspring may be properly produced.
We shall always worship with various sacrifices accompanied by complete sacrificial fees; thus remaining steadfast, we shall accomplish both this world and the next.
Having heard that, the king was delighted and said, "So be it," and thereafter, when a favorable day arrived, he summoned numerous artisans.
He caused a city to be constructed, crowded with many walls, provided with ramparts and moats, and beautifully adorned with gate-towers.
Then, in the midst of those sixty-eight brahmins, the best of kings constructed sixty-eight very large houses.
They were frequented by rutting elephants, provided with oblong ponds, and endowed with domestic gardens, just like the palaces of kings.
Having done so, and then having filled [the area] with heaps of jewels and other [valuables], he immediately thereafter gave them sixty-eight villages.
Then, having summoned all his sons and grandsons before him, he spoke in a resonant voice: "Listen to me as I speak."
This city, together with these villages, has been given by me to these eminent Brahmins with a mind purified by faith. (15)
Therefore, protection must be provided so that no harm whatsoever occurs, nor any suffering or defeat for these foremost of Brahmins. (16)
"Whosoever shall please these [deities], whether he be born of our lineage or another king, he will surely attain the highest prosperity. (17)

And whoever shall bring these men, who are joined with offenses, to distress, or shall subject them to various afflictions or humiliations—he, being defeated by his enemies and surrounded by manifold diseases, [shall suffer]. (18)
In this world, having encountered extremely terrible afflictions such as separation from loved ones, he will go to the fierce hells, such as Raurava and others.
