Whenever liquor has been drunk by a Brahmin even once through ignorance, he becomes purified by drinking an amount of clarified butter equal in measure to that [liquor], which is like fire.
Thus has all the expiation for the sake of purification been declared to you; O best of the twice-born, if you are able to perform it, then do so.
Parāvasu said: "O best of the twice-born, I have drunk but a single mouthful of liquor; I shall drink only that much ghee which has been made as hot as fire. (39)
"Right this very day, for the purification of my own body, [I shall act] by means of your command. And Viśvāvasu, having heard those words which were like a thunderbolt falling, [acted accordingly].
Then, deeply distressed, shedding profuse tears and with a voice faltering with sobs, he spoke thus to the son of the brahmins.
I shall give even my entire possessions for the purification of this son; however, I will by no means allow him to perform an expiatory rite.
"O son, let it not be that I become one unworthy of trust or excluded from the row of eaters, along with my sons; or else, I shall abandon this very place—do not act in such a manner. (43)
Having heard those words of his father, which were most obstructive to his penance, the son spoke these affectionate words.
"O father, abandon your affection for me; do not create an obstacle for me. I shall perform the penance; this is the firm resolve I have made. (45)
The mother said: "O son, if you must perform an expiation for the sake of purification, then I shall enter the fire before you, together with your husband."
I am truly unable to behold you drinking ghee like fire; if this be not so, I swear it by my own life. (47)
The father said: "What has been spoken by your mother is fitting and likewise for your benefit; this is indeed my own consent as well, and I shall do it without a doubt. (48)
Sūta said: In the meantime, all those friends of his who were present there—
Having heard that account, they arrived there filled with grief.
And they addressed the Fire-god, together with his wife, with various words—he who was tormented by grief for his son and had resolved upon death. || 5 ||
They sought to awaken their son for the sake of performing an expiation, but at that time they were unable to turn him back easily.
And both of them, father and son, were intent on giving up their lives.
Then they went to the site where the Omniscient One resided—where the illustrious Bhartṛyajña, the dispeller of all doubts, was staying. (53)
They related to him everything concerning the origin of Parāvasu—the account arising from the drinking of wine that had been told by his friends.

Furthermore, the expiation proclaimed by the followers of the Smṛtis as being performed with laughter, as well as the ritual resolve (saṃkalpa) of Viśvāvasu involving the procurement of fire—these [he recounted].
Having reported the suffering that had befallen him along with his wife and friends, he spoke to the king with humility.
Whether it be past, present, or even what may be future—there is nothing unknown to you; we know all this.
And now this entire city, on account of Viśvāvasu, has fallen into a state of extreme peril; therefore, he has come into your presence. (58)
Therefore, O illustrious one, tell me if there is indeed any other expiation for this twice-born man to purify himself from the drinking of liquor. (59)
"Indeed, there is nothing arising from the Vedas that is unknown to you. Then Bhartṛyajña, laughing loudly, spoke these words: (60)
"Even though there exists a means that brings happiness for the sake of this Brahmin's purification, it is as if it does not exist; such is the conviction established in my mind. (61)

The Brāhmaṇas said: "O high-minded one, this statement contains a contradiction between what precedes and what follows; how can it both exist and not exist? Therefore, you ought to explain this. A great wonder has arisen among all of us twice-born ones. (62)
Bhartṛyajña said: Whatever flaw there may be in recitation, whatever flaw in austerity, and whatever flaw in the performance of a sacrifice—all that becomes flawless if the Brāhmaṇas so desire. (63)
Whatever statement the gods of the earth utter, saying "it is flawless," especially those born of Nāgara lineage, it is exactly so and not otherwise.
And likewise, that which has been uttered by those assembled in the Brahma-hall must not be understood otherwise, even as a joke, for it is without [need for] further recollection.
Thus was this Parāvasu addressed by his friends with a sense of humor.
If, having grasped the breasts of Ratnavatī, he tastes her lower lip, that shall be my purification arising from the drinking of liquor. (67)
I have declared this means for bringing happiness to this brahmin; if he performs it according to the doctrine of Parāśara, he becomes purified.
The Brāhmaṇas said: "If the king, who is devoted to envy, hears these words, he will surely carry out the slaughter of all the Brāhmaṇas; otherwise, it would be different. (69)
Therefore, let this Brahmin Parāvasu do what he desires; accompanied by his mother and father, we shall go home.
Bhartṛyajña said: That king was wise, learned, and devoted to all duties; he was a devotee of the gods and the twice-born, and an expert in all the scriptures.
Therefore, let all the citizens go with me to his house.
Placing the one who had gone to the middle in front, and with his face turned toward that [other] person, let them relate the account arising from the drinking of liquor.
And that which was spoken by the companions out of a spirit of jest regarding Parāvasu, as well as the words originating from Parāśara, are beyond the reach of memory.
Having heard that, O protector of the earth, if he becomes possessed by envy and greed, then I shall establish him on the path of the righteous.
Sūta said: Then all those citizens attained supreme satisfaction, honoring Bhartṛyajña with various shouts of "Well done! (sādhuvāda).
Accompanied by him alone, having quickly placed that one who had mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas—who was born at Gartātīrtha—in the middle, [he proceeded].

He was one who knew the sacred traditions and understood their characteristics; he had maintained the sacred fires, was illustrious, a performer of many sacrifices, and remained steadfast in the opinion of Bhartṛyajña.
Formerly, even by King Ānarta—who had fallen from heaven and was the ancient progenitor of Karṇotpalā—this [rite] was indeed performed in the past.
It was installed in this place at Camatkārapura out of respect for the brahmins, so that the objectives of all twice-born men might be accomplished.
And likewise, there were others from Camatkārapura, including one named Haribhadra who was accompanied by Bhartṛyajña. (81)
Having done so, all those citizens approached the palace gate, taking Parāvasu along with his mother and father.
Then the gatekeeper, having gone quickly, announced to the king those brahmins accompanied by Haribhadra, the son of Bhartṛyajña.
And Ānarta, having heard that they had arrived at the palace gate, then went out to meet them accompanied by his family priest.
Having offered the guest-water (arghya), the honey-mixture (madhuparka), a seat (viṣṭara), and a cow, the king first [honored] Bhartṛyajña and then indeed Haribhadra.
Then, four twice-born men with mung beans in their hands, as well as others, having first uttered the supreme words of benediction consisting of the Ṛg, Yajur, and Sāma Vedas— || 86 ||
Having reached the assembly hall, he seated them all upon excellent golden seats, duly and in proper order.
When they had all thus taken their seats, the lord of the earth sat upon the surface of the ground and spoke with palms joined in reverence.
"I am blessed and I am graced, since this entire city-dwelling populace, together with Bhartṛyajña, has come to my home. (89)
Therefore, let the world command me as to what task I should perform for you; even that which is not to be given, I shall now bestow upon one who has come to my home.
"I shall go even where I ought not to go, and I shall do even what ought not to be done. Having heard that, Haribhadra rose up with great haste.
He questioned the Bahvṛcas first regarding that matter, and immediately after them the Adhvaryus and the Chāndogyas; and he was then permitted by them.

Let the Prāṇarudras now recite, and let the Bahvṛcas recite the Jīvasūkta; and let there be the performance of the Savana sacrifice for these [deities], beginning with Earth, as was performed in the past.
Let all the Adhvaryus and the Chāndogyas recite individually; let them recite it thoroughly, joined with the flowing honey, for the sake of success.
O best of the twice-born, having been thus addressed by him according to the opinion of Bhartṛyajña, they questioned that wise man about everything he had explained.
Then, at the conclusion of the recitation, the mediator respectfully related to that king the account concerning the birth of Parāvasu.
Just as he drank the liquor, just as his friends conversed, and just as the expiation consisting of ghee was prescribed by those learned in the Smṛtis; || 97 ||
Having heard how all the twice-born were brought by Bhartṛyajña, the king was delighted and, with palms joined in reverence, spoke: || 98 ||
I am blessed and I have performed meritorious deeds, since these Nāgara twice-born ones have shown me this great favor for the sake of protecting three Brāhmaṇas. (99)
"Blessed is this daughter of mine; she herself shall protect these three Brahmins who have indeed resolved upon death. (100)
Then, O twice-born ones, he had that maiden brought at that very moment and, while she was seated in the midst of the assembly, he presented her to the brāhmaṇas.
"O best of the twice-born, this maiden has been brought by me at your word; let that brahmin perform whatever was commanded by Bhartṛyajña. (102)
Then, having brought that Brāhmaṇa Parāvasu there, Bhartṛyajña spoke these words in the presence of the maiden: || 103 ||
If you consider this maiden as your mother in your mind, then, by tasting her lower lip, you will attain success.
O Parāvasu, if you become intent on passion and devoted to tasting [it], then your mouth will turn red. 105.
Furthermore, milk will indeed come from a pure [cow], of this there is no doubt. || 106 ||
If, through the touch of your breasts and hands, milk should flow, then that purity of yours is to be recognized; otherwise, there will be blood. (107)
Having spoken thus, that twice-born man then said to the maiden: "O daughter, look upon this most excellent of Brahmins as you would a son."
For it is traditionally taught that one attains purification by tasting the lips of such a woman and by touching her breasts; therefore, an expiation must be performed. (109)
This [must be done] for this lord of brahmins by his companions with words of jest, so that he may attain purity; otherwise, he will meet his death.
Sūta said: Having agreed, saying "So be it," she spoke to him with bashfulness: "Come, my child; perform an expiation for the sake of purification."
Having assumed the state of a mother, I conceived you as my son; he too, regarding her as his mother, came into her presence.
And he touched her breasts while the whole world looked on; and as soon as she was touched by those two breasts, O best of the twice-born, at that very moment—
When a stream of milk, resembling jasmine, the moon, and snow, had issued forth.
Then, as soon as that twice-born man tasted her lips, milk of such a form issued forth from her mouth.
In the meantime, all the twice-born men clapped their hands, repeatedly declaring, "This king is a pure Brāhmaṇa! || 116 ||
He too, having circumambulated that maiden again and again, and having prostrated, said: "Forgive me, O Mother, you who are affectionate toward your son. (117)
Having seen that great marvel, Ānarta, filled with wonder, praised Bhaṭṛyajña, the bestower of atonement.
"Oh, how exceedingly fortunate am I, that such Brahmins, all hailing from Camatkārapura, have come to my home! (119)
And so, such a maiden as this, indeed extraordinary in her conduct, the highly fortunate Ratnāvatī, is endowed with truthfulness and purity.
Likewise, this Brāhmaṇa Parāvasu is not at all an ordinary man, since he remained unperturbed even after encountering such a maiden as ours. (121)
Having spoken thus and dismissed those brahmins, that best of kings took the maiden and then departed for his inner apartments.
Then all those citizens established a rule: "From this day forward, whatever prostitute shall come to reside in this place... (123)
She must not keep wine or meat in her house under any circumstances; for here, the wicked sons of the city-dwellers are constantly corrupting [her]. (124)
Now, she who, transgressing the established rule, shall wear it, is to be punished and banished from this place; after death, she shall partake in the fruit of her sin.
Then, by means of the central pillar of the Audumbarī tree, three claps were given.

Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-seventh chapter, titled "The Description of the Account of Parāvasu’s Performance of Atonement," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. 197.
Sūta said: At that very time, the lord of Daśārṇa arrived at that place for the purpose of marrying Ratnavatī.
Having heard the account of Ratnavatī’s origin there, he conceived a supreme detachment and set out toward his own city.
Having heard that the king was setting out toward his own city of Ānarta, the hunter then followed behind him for the sake of killing him.
Then, having approached him, he said: "O King, why have you departed without performing my marriage and without taking a wife?"
Daśārṇa said: "This daughter of yours has been defiled; she is no longer a maiden, since her lower lip has been drunk by another and likewise her breasts have been pressed."
She who was known as Punarbhū has become your daughter; may that Punarbhū give birth to a son for you at some time, by whatever means possible.
He undoubtedly causes ten ancestors, ten descendants, and likewise the twenty-first person—himself—to fall.
"O King, I will not give my daughter to you," the lord of Daśārṇa then said, speaking thus without any courtesy.
Although he was enticed with various gifts, beginning with elephants, horses, and chariots, he disregarded the protector of the earth and set out toward his own city.
Then Anarta, having reached his home, was deeply distressed; filled with grief, he related to his wife, his daughter, and his ministers that account which had been told to him by the king. (10)
They said: "There are kings on the surface of the earth beyond counting, endowed with beauty, possessed of youth, and equipped with elephants, horses, and chariots."
"O Lord, give your own daughter to one of them; do not set your mind on despair, nor fall under the sway of sorrow. (12)
And Ānarta, having heard those words of theirs which were so full of grief, then spoke with a joyful soul to all of them, led by his ministers. (13)
And to that maiden standing there, he spoke with most beautiful conciliation: "Daughter, you have seen all the protectors of the earth depicted in these paintings."
"O beautiful one, choose some other king from among them, whoever brings satisfaction to your heart when he comes within the range of your vision. (15)
Ratnāvatī said: "I shall by no means choose any other husband except for the lord of Daśārṇa; hear now the reason for this. (16)
Kings speak but once; twice-born brahmins speak but once; daughters are given in marriage but once—these three things happen only once, each time.
Knowing this, O father, you ought not to give me to another king, for by doing so, this eternal dharma would not be maintained.
Ānarta said: "I gave you away to the lord of Daśārṇa by word alone; you have not been taken by the hand in the presence of Brahmins, fire, and gurus. (19)
Therefore, daughter, tell me how he became your husband. || 20 ||
Ratnāvatī said: "Since a task is first conceived by the mind, it is subsequently expressed through speech, and thereafter it is carried out through action. (21)

"O Lord, it is said that in the past this self of mine was given to him by my mind, and likewise I was given to him by you through your word. Therefore, tell me why he should not be my husband, or say whatever you deem appropriate. (22)
Therefore, I shall practice asceticism, observing the vow of lifelong maidenhood; I will not take another husband—this is the firm resolve I have made.
Having heard those terrible words, her mother Mṛgāvatī, distressed and with eyes filled with tears, spoke these words.
"Do not, my daughter, commit such a rash act for the sake of asceticism by any means; you are but a young girl with delicate limbs, always accustomed to happiness. (25)
"How, O blameless one, are you able to perform asceticism, subsisting on roots, tubers, and fruits, and wearing garments of bark and rags? (26)
Therefore, I shall give you to some eminent king.
This is your friend named Brāhmaṇī, who is highly esteemed; remaining in her maidenhood, she awaits your marriage. (28)
"O bride, that king in whose palace you shall go to be wed—this woman will become the wife of that king's domestic priest. (29)
Ratnāvatī said: "If you desire my life for my sake, O seeker of a son, you must never again speak such words anywhere. (30)
Or else, you will create an obstacle to my asceticism for the sake of forceful seizure. (31)
"Therefore, having consumed a potent poison, I shall cast off my body; or I shall cut out my tongue, or I shall enter the water. (32)
Having thus made her resolve and spoken to her mother at that time, she—
Then, having respectfully embraced her esteemed friend, the Brahmin woman, and having joined her palms in reverence, she spoke to that maiden.
"Go, O auspicious one; you have been sent by me to your father's palace, so that your father may bestow [me] upon that high-souled Nāga. (35)
Forgive me for any harsh words that I have ever spoken to you; and whatever has been said by you to me, that too has certainly been forgiven by me.
The Brāhmaṇa woman said: "A girl of eight years is Gaurī, one of nine years is Rohiṇī, and one of ten years is Kanyā; beyond that age, she is Rajasvalā (menstruating)."
O fair-faced one, my maidenhood has been destroyed through contact with you; the sixteenth year has arrived, endowed with the characteristics of womanhood. (38)
"O fair-faced one, no citizen here will take my hand in marriage; however, for the sake of memory, I shall speak what is about to be said while I am awake. (39)
That pitiless man who marries a maiden while she is in her menses shall, by obtaining offspring from her, cause ten generations of men to fall.
But that pitiless father who bestows a daughter while she is in her menses shall undoubtedly cause the downfall of ten ancestors and ten descendants. (41)
Therefore, O auspicious lady, I shall perform penance together with you; for I have no concern whatsoever with my father or my mother.
Sūta said: O best of the twice-born, having thus made their resolve, the two maidens went to where the great sage Bhartṛyajña was personally stationed.
He was established in a beautiful and auspicious site for a dwelling, which contained all sacred fords; by the power of his asceticism, anger was never seen in him.
For some mortal here or there, or even for one born as an animal, mongooses play with serpents and cats with mice.

O auspicious ones, having gone there to Bhartṛyajña as he sat comfortably, the deer together with the leopards and the crows together with the owls stood with palms joined in reverence and spoke with humility. (46)
The Brāhmaṇī said: "I have come here together with my friend, this princess, for the sake of penance at your feet; therefore, tell me the procedure for that penance. (47)
Tell me, O Mahāmati, so that I may perform all of that.
Bhartṛyajña said: I shall describe to you separately the rules for the practice of austerity, by which liberation is attained—how much more so the abode of the gods! || 49 ||
One should perform Cāndrāyaṇa penances, Kṛcchras, and likewise Sāntapana penances; furthermore, one should eat only at the sixth meal-time, or even on alternate days.
The Brahmakūrca, the three-night fast, eating once a day, and eating unasked for food—all these have been established by the Creator as gateways to austerity.

One should perform all tasks according to one's own capacity, free from attachment and aversion; and every fruit should be desired by all, O daughter, for then one attains that perfection which has always resided in the mind.
When equanimity toward enemy and friend, as well as toward a clod of earth and a jewel, arises in the mind, then one shall attain liberation. || 53 ||
He who, having undertaken the assumption of the sectarian mark (liṅga), then becomes intent on anger—for him all that is indeed in vain, just like an oblation poured into ashes. || 54 ||
Sūta said: Having promised "So be it," that Brāhmaṇī, accompanied by Ratnāvatī, then went to a certain reservoir of water.
It was filled with clear water and adorned with clusters of lotuses; thereupon, he performed the Cāndrāyaṇa, the first vow of his ascetic penance.
Then she performed the Kṛcchra vow and the Sāṃtapana vow; for three years, she ate only at every sixth meal-time.
After fasting for three nights, she likewise spent three years fasting on alternate days; in this manner, she passed those three years.
In the winter, that ascetic woman remained standing in the midst of water; in the summer, that illustrious lady practiced the penance of the five fires.
When the rainy season arrived, that virtuous woman became without support; she meditated day and night upon Janārdana, the God of gods.
O best of the twice-born, whatever vow that virtuous Brahmin woman had previously performed, the princess, filled with supreme joy, undertook that very same vow upon reaching another body of water.
Then for a hundred and fifty years she subsisted on fruits; thereafter, she remained for an equal period subsisting on withered leaves.
Then she subsisted on water alone for six hundred years, and thereafter she lived for a thousand years subsisting on air alone.
O best of the twice-born, in whatever measure that maiden performed penance, in that same measure her unsurpassed increase of splendor occurred.
At that very time, however, the Blessed One whose crest is the moon—
With a serene soul, he came within her range along with Gaurī; then, in a voice as deep as a thundercloud, he spoke these words.
"O child, at my word, cease your ascetic penance; ask for whatever your heart desires, so that I may grant it all to you. (67)
The Brahmin woman said: "O Śaṅkara, this alone is my greatest desire—that you have been seen by me, for even in a dream, O Lord, a vision of you is difficult for men to obtain. (68)
The Blessed One said: "O woman of great asceticism, my sight shall never be in vain for you in any way. Therefore, choose a boon—blessings upon you—so that I may grant it to you."
The Brāhmaṇa’s wife said: "This is my virtuous and noble friend, the illustrious princess renowned by the name Ratnāvatī; she is dearer to me than my own life. (70)

"Even though she remains in the womb of a Śūdra, she has performed austerities equal to mine. O Lord of the World, if she should indeed turn back from her penance, I shall today bring about that cessation of her asceticism without any doubt. (71)
"O Lord of the Gods, out of affection for her, I have abandoned my husband; therefore, O God, grant her the boon that resides in her heart. (72)

Sūta said: Having heard those words of hers, the moon-crested Lord spoke to that princess with a voice as deep as a thundercloud: "O child, at my word, you ought to abandon your ascetic penance today."
"Choose a boon, O auspicious lady, that has always resided in your mind; O beautiful woman, I shall grant it to you now, even if it be something that ought not to be given. (74)
Ratnāvatī said: "This meritorious reservoir of water is adorned with clusters of lotuses. (75)
"Wherever this virtuous Brāhmaṇī dwells, eternally established in austerity, let this sacred ford (tīrtha) attain renown by her name. (76)
O God of gods, may he who performs a bath here, endowed with supreme faith, always have his residence in Triviṣṭapa. || 77 ||
"Let that which belongs to me arise under my name as 'Śūdrā'; let it attain a power equal to that of the sacred ford. (78)
"From our very youth, we have constantly performed great austerities; thus, you, the best of gods, were to be propitiated by us through speech, mind, and action. (79)
At that very moment, O brahmins, a Liṅga of Maheśvara, resembling the sun, emerged, having pierced through the surface of the earth.
Then the god Maheśvara himself, who is affectionate toward his devotees, being pleased by their excellent penance, spoke to them with respect.
These two sacred fords shall become renowned even throughout the three worlds; one shall be named Śūdrī, yours, and the other your friend, Brāhmaṇī.
"Whoever, endowed with faith, bathes in both of these sacred fords (tīrthas), takes lotuses from you and her own pure water, and having bathed this Liṅga of mine, shall worship it. (83)
Later, on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight in the month of Caitra, when it falls on a Monday, he shall become long-lived by means of lotuses. (84)
Even if one were a perpetrator of great evil, they would be completely liberated from all sins.
Having spoken thus, the Blessed One vanished from that place; meanwhile, both friends remained there constantly engaged in ascetic penance.
For as long as a hundred kalpas, they have been free from old age and death; even today, they are seen in the sky in the form of stars.
From that time forward, that pair of holy fords became renowned upon the earth; then, having come from afar, a man should perform his immersion in those two.
Having worshipped that liṅga, one then goes to the abode of the gods; even if burdened with great sins, this occurs through its power without a doubt. (89)
In the meantime, among mortals, the performance of dharma was lost—namely, that which arises from sacrifice, giving, and the worship of the gods. (90)
Likewise, the entire heaven was pervaded by humans filled with rivalry, together with gods residing in celestial chariots and attended by throngs of apsarases.
At that very time, however, Dharmarāja arrived where Brahmā resided in the world of Brahmā, where the sound of the Vedas resounded. || 92 ||
Distressed and dejected, he spoke after casting two leaves before him—one arising from sin and the other arising from merit. (93)
That which was painted by Citra and likewise that other by Vicitra—the pair of Devatīrthas—resides in the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara.
There is a [liṅga] called Śūdra belonging to the Brāhmaṇīs, and likewise another adorned with lotuses; furthermore, there is a great and meritorious Māheśvara liṅga located there.
Furthermore, by the power of those three, all human beings—even those joined with sin—go to the abode of the gods.
All my hells, including Raurava and the others, have become empty. || 97 ||
No one performed sacrifice, nor gave gifts, nor offered libations to the gods, the ancestors, and especially to human beings. || 98 ||
Therefore, I have relinquished all authority that arose from you; henceforth, appoint someone else who is most capable in that regard.
"All this [world] is established as immeasurable; these two leaves of mine are likewise. Having heard that, the Lotus-born One summoned Śatakratu and said:
"O Śakra, having gone very swiftly to the mortal world at my command, [inform them of] the two unsurpassed holy sites (tīrtha) located in the field of Hāṭakeśvara. || 101 ||
"Destroy quickly that most excellent Linga known as Śūdrī, which is situated there as 'Brāhmaṇī,' by raining down a shower of dust. (102)
Sūta said: Having heard that, Śakra then went quickly to the surface of the earth and filled both the holy site and the liṅga with dust.
Even now, in this Kali age, having taken excellent clay with both hands and bathed, one should apply the *tilaka* for the purification of all sins. (104)

When the fourteenth day arrives and it falls on a Monday, if one endowed with supreme faith performs the Śrāddha rite on both [days], what need has he for a Śrāddha at Gayā? Thus spoke Svāyambhuva Manu. (105)
O best of the twice-born, all this that I was asked by you has been related; namely, how she became a Brāhmaṇa woman and how the other became a Śūdra woman.
O best of the twice-born, whoever hears this with devotion or recites it shall also be liberated from the sins born of that day; there is no doubt in this matter. || 107 ||
Thus, what man has not attained perfection by worshipping that *liṅga*? He became long-lived, such as no other is found here. (108)
The sages said: "O Sūta, it is heard that thirty-five million sacred fords (tīrthas) exist here upon the surface of the earth, being recounted in their entirety by the lords of sages."
O illustrious one, how may the fruit arising from bathing at all sacred fords be obtained by those of short lifespan when the Kali age has arrived? (2)
Sūta said: Three sacred fields (kṣetra) are proclaimed here, as well as three great forests (araṇya); likewise, there are three cities, three groves, and three villages. || 3 ||
Likewise, there is another triad of sacred fords (tīrtha) accompanied by a triad of mountains, as well as a triad of great rivers that destroys all sins.
O Brahmins, it is situated in the mortal world and bestows the fruit of all holy fords (tīrthas); whoever bathes in all of these shall obtain the fruit of them all.
Prajāpati has declared this regarding those numbering twenty-four: he who bathes at a single triad obtains the fruit of all the triads.
The sages said:
What are the three fields here, and what are the forests? O highly fortunate one, which three cities are renowned, and what are the groves?
O Sūta, tell us in detail by name all those villages, sacred fords, mountains, and rivers.
Sūta said:
The first and most excellent sacred field is renowned as Kurukṣetra; the second is proclaimed to be the field born of Hāṭakeśvara.
The third sacred field, O best of the twice-born, is indeed Prābhāsika; these three fields are meritorious and destroy all sins.
Having beheld [them] according to the prescribed rule, a person is liberated from sin; whoever, meditating upon whatever desire, visits these sacred fields with devotion. (11)
O twice-born ones, he who performs a bath there obtains his desired fruit born of the mind; he becomes as one who has bathed in all twenty-four sacred measures.
O twice-born ones, among them, one is the Puṣkarāraṇya, and Naimiṣāraṇya as well; Dharmāraṇya is proclaimed as the third of these.
And he who bathes in these three shall become a partaker of a twenty-fourth share.
Vārāṇasī is one city, the second is the city of Dvārakā, and the third is known as Avantī, renowned throughout the three worlds. (15)
The man who bathes in these becomes a partaker of twenty-four [merits]. || 16 ||
Vṛndāvana is one forest, the second is Khāṇḍava forest, and the third, renowned on the surface of the earth, is Dvaitavana.
And whoever bathes in these three shall obtain a twenty-fourth part [of the merit]. || 18 ||
Kalpagrāma is remembered as the first, Śāligrāma the second, and Nandigrāma is renowned as the third, O best of the twice-born. (19)
And he who bathes in these three shall become a partaker of a twenty-fourth share.
One is known as Agnitīrtha, another is Śuklatīrtha, and the third is Pitṛtīrtha, which is exceedingly dear to the ancestors.
And he who bathes in these three shall obtain a share in twenty-four.
Śrīparvata is remembered as the first, Arbuda as the second, and the third is the one known here as Raivata; these are the most excellent of mountains. (23)
And whoever bathes in these three becomes a partaker of twenty-four.
The Gaṅgā river is remembered as the first, and the one called Narmadā is the second; the third river is the Sarasvatī, which originates from the Plakṣa tree.
Whoever bathes in all of these shall become a partaker of the merit of twenty-four.
Indeed, whatever man performs his ablutions in all of these, he shall obtain the entire fruit of three and a half crores [of such acts]. || 27 ||
And whatever man bathes in one [of these], he shall obtain the fruit of all three.
O best of the twice-born, all this that I was asked by you has been related; [namely], the merit arising from sacred fords (tīrthas) which is obtained by men on earth in brief.
"Now, what indeed shall I say to you? Speak that without delay."
The sages said:
O son of Sūta, you have described to us in great detail all those sacred fords that exist in the holy field of Hāṭakeśvara.
Likewise, these very sense-bases (āyatana) are devoid of numerical reckoning; even in a hundred years, it is impossible to perform a ritual bath here.
O noble-minded one, among all those [places], a mortal should clearly perceive them as the very abodes of the deities according to the prescribed rule. (33)
The prosperity resulting from bathing on that very day is proclaimed; yet even then, mortals are declared to be short-lived. (34)
In the Tretā and Dvāpara ages as well, and even more so now that the Kali age has arrived—O son of Sūta, knowing that human beings are thus short-lived—(35)
And how may those who are especially destitute obtain the fruit arising from bathing at all sacred fords, or even that born from the sight of the gods? (36)
Is there some means here, whether divine or even human, by which merit may accrue to all of them with ease? (37)
Sūta said: Regarding this matter, in ancient times the great sage Viśvāmitra was questioned after King Ānarta had approached his hermitage.
The King said: "O Blessed One, the sacred fords here are beyond numbering; the procedure for bathing in all of them has been described individually. (39)
In certain months, on specific days of the week, and on particular dates, gifts have been prescribed by the best of sages, just as the rules for ritual bathing have been prescribed.
O Sage, the vision of the gods has also been proclaimed separately; it is not possible for anyone to obtain the fruit of all of them at once.
Not even in a hundred years, much less in a few short days; therefore, O illustrious one, tell us the means for embodied beings to attain happiness.
And by bathing at even a single sacred ford, a human being obtains the entire fruit arising from bathing at all sacred fords whatsoever. (43)
Likewise, O best of the twice-born, when even a single deity is seen, the fruit arising from that vision for men will be equal to the vision of all the gods.
Sūta said: Having heard that and meditated for a very long time, the great sage Viśvāmitra spoke: "Listen, O Indra among kings; I shall tell you the secret along with its mysteries. (45)

O King, there are four preeminent and principal holy fords (tīrthas) here; O monarch, when one performs a ritual bath and subsequently a śrāddha ceremony at these, one obtains the fruit arising from bathing at all holy fords whatsoever. (46)
Likewise, twenty-seven Liṅgas are situated right here, beginning with Siddheśvara; they are the destroyers of all sins.
When all of these have been seen with a mind purified by devotion, the fruit arising from the vision of all the gods shall be attained.
If even a single most excellent deity among them is beheld or worshipped, the worship of all twenty-seven liṅgas has been performed by him. (49)
The King said: O holy sage, which are the four principal sacred sites there, by bathing properly in which a man obtains the fruit of all [pilgrimages]? (50)
Viśvāmitra said: Here there is a meritorious little well (kūpikā) in which Gayā resides on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight as well as on the new moon day. || 51 ||
Especially, O highly fortunate one, while the sun was situated in Virgo, we became despondent with the various kinds of Śrāddha rites performed by the people of the earth.
Whoever performs a śrāddha ceremony there, endowed with perfect faith, [attains the highest reward]. || 53 ||
On that day, O Indra among kings, he causes his ancestors to cross over; likewise, there is a second sacred ford (tīrtha) known as Śaṅkhatīrtha.
Having bathed there, the man who then beholds Śaṅkheśvara on the first day of the month of Māgha obtains the fruit of all [the rites]. || 55 ||
Likewise, this third holy site named after me has attained preeminence; having bathed here, whoever beholds Hara established by me, [shall attain the highest goal]. (56)
On the eighth day of the bright fortnight of the month of Nabhasya, he obtains the fruit of all [pilgrimages] at the shrine named Viśvāmitreśvara. || 57 ||

The fourth is known as Śakratīrtha, the ornament of children; having bathed there for five days and beheld Śakreśvara on the eighth day of the bright fortnight of Āśvina, one obtains the fruit of all [pilgrimages].
The king said: "O Brahmin, O highly fortunate one, tell me in detail the ritual procedure and the origin of Gayākūpī; my faith is very great. (59)
Viśvāmitra said: When the new moon day arrives, and the sun has entered the sign of Virgo, he who performs a śrāddha with devotion shall deliver his own ancestors.
By means of pure twice-born men born in that place according to the ritual of Bhartṛyajña; for that man who, having abandoned the ritual of Bhartṛyajña, performs it by another rite, || 61 ||

If a foolish-souled person performs a śrāddha ceremony devoid of brahmins born in that sacred place (sthānaja), or even if they are from that place but are impure, that rite shall go to futility for him.

Just as rain falls upon saline soil, so too is this truth spoken by me; for just as a dance before a blind man or a song for one who is deaf is in vain, so too does it become useless when performed by Brahmins born in other places. 63.
O best of the twice-born, one should have the śrāddha performed even by ignorant brāhmaṇas; those who have mastered the four Vedas should be rejected if they originate from another place.

Whether in a rite for the ancestors or especially in a soma-sacrifice, if a man who has traveled to another country performs a śrāddha, he must perform it with Vaiśvānara at the forefront; no other [deity] is prescribed for a twice-born man.

O best of the twice-born, having seated the darbha-representatives, one should perform the śrāddha; sacrificial fees and food should be given even after a long time to those who were present at the site.
O best of kings, just as a jar filled with the five products of the cow becomes utterly defiled by the falling of even a single drop of liquor, so it is here.
O King, even if only one outsider is seated among many [invited guests], that śrāddha incurs a fault.

Even one born of noble lineage, though he may be a knower of the four Vedas, if he is not possessed of purity, he will destroy a Śrāddha even when it is performed in the midst of many pure persons. (69)
Therefore, with every effort, one should bring a pure Brāhmaṇa.

Even if he is a local resident or a fool, and even in the absence of those possessed of virtues, one who has a missing limb or an extra limb, or one who is defiled—none other than these should be excluded. (71)

O best of kings, he who desires his own welfare must always strive diligently to invite a Brahmin of noble lineage for the giving away of a daughter in marriage as well as for the Śrāddha ceremony; provided, however, that he too is endowed with purity. (72)
Just as the Aśvattha is among trees, and Hari is among the gods, so too is one born of the eight families the most excellent among Brahmins of noble birth and lineage. (73)
Just as the thunderbolt is among weapons and the ocean is among bodies of water, so too is one born of the eight families the most excellent among Brahmins of noble lineage.
Just as Uccaiḥśravas is among horses and the vehicle of Śakra is among elephants, so too is one born of the eight families the best among Brahmins of noble status and lineage.
Just as the Gaṅgā is among rivers and Arundhatī is among virtuous women, so too is the Aṣṭakulika Brāhmaṇa considered the most excellent among those born in that place.
Just as the sun is among the planets and the moon is among the stars, so too is the Aṣṭakulika remembered as the most excellent among the Brahmins born in their respective stations. (77)
Just as Meru is among mountains and the twice-born brahmin is supreme among bipeds, so too is the Aṣṭakulika the most excellent among brahmins born of their respective stations.
Just as Garuḍa is among birds and the lion among those dwelling in the forest, so too is the one of the eight lineages (Aṣṭakulika) the most excellent among Brahmins born of that place.
Knowing this, O King, one should diligently employ those born of the eight families in funeral rites (śrāddha), sacrifices (yajña), and especially in the giving away of a daughter in marriage.
O King, seeing that the eight ancestors have arrived at the base of the altar, his forefathers dance and his grandfathers roar with joy.
Again they spoke with great joy: "What will our grandson give us—water mixed with *darbha* grass and sesame seeds, offered with the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*apasavya*)? (82)
The King said: "O high-minded one, tell me why this preeminence arising from the eight families, which you have described, belongs to all the Nāgaras. (83)
For indeed, O best of the twice-born, there will not be even a slight cause for this here.
Viśvāmitra said: "O great king, this word which you have spoken is true; there are other citizens as well who have reached the further shore of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences. (85)
O King, they are worthy of ancestral rites (śrāddha), fit for sacrifice, and especially suitable for marriage; moreover, they were established there by Indra himself.
Because they were preeminent among all [the temples] by the citizens as well as in their entirety, they attained great honor, especially in this very place. || 87 ||
Therefore, the śrāddha ceremony should be performed by Brahmins born of the eight families; however, in their absence, it should be performed by those born of the Nāgara lineage.
This boundary was indeed established by the high-souled Bhartṛyajña, even against the twice-born who had mastered the four Vedas produced in other places. (89)
But whoever shall perform a śrāddha or a sacrifice here by means of anyone other than a Nāgara Brahmin, that [act] of his will be in vain. (90)
The king said: "There are other various brahmins who have mastered the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas—those born in the Middle Country who are peaceful, as well as others originating from sacred fords."

Those who were excluded by Bhartṛyajña from the Śrāddha and especially from the sacrifice—those with deficient limbs, those with redundant limbs, those who are doubly naked, and those with blackened teeth; || 92 ||
Those with deformed nails, those afflicted with leprosy, and even fools who are censured—by whom were they declared worthy of the śrāddha? Tell me this, for it is a doubt of mine. (93)
Viśvāmitra said: O tiger among men, I shall recount many reasons why Camatkāra’s wife fell because of her gift. (94)
Through the very acceptance of women when the Brahmins had gone abroad, a separation arose from that point on, designated as "external" and "internal. (95)
Then, as if by an enraged serpent, they were cursed by Durvāsas; fallen forever by that curse through their pride in learning and wealth. (96)
O King, when Kuśa had attained the kingdom, a great fear among the Rākṣasas was reported by the subjects to that high-souled monarch. (97)
Then a messenger was dispatched to Laṅkā for Vibhīṣaṇa, and he reported everything regarding the emergence of fear among the subjects. 98.
Having paid homage to the command of Kuśa and recollecting the deeds of Rāma, he surveyed the city of Laṅkā by the order of Rāma.
All those who caused the calamity have perished in the ten directions; indeed, out of great fear, they have fled to the world of the Gandharvas.
Unable to remain there due to the fear of Vibhīṣaṇa, they reached the earth and found many places to stay.
Out of great fear, however, within the very teaching of Kuśa, they assembled there having assumed the forms of brahmins.
And due to the greatness of the Vāḍavas, they were unable to remain in their midst; having fallen, they went to Camatkārapura, the abode of those who have fallen from their status. || 103 ||
Then, by means of their mastery of illusion, wealth, and knowledge, they devoured those who were situated among them. || 104 ||
From that time forward, they all attained the state of Rākṣasas, and at every step they performed even cruel deeds.
Therefore, O King, tiger among men, they must be avoided with every effort and by all means at a śrāddha or a sacrifice; for they cause one to fall into hell. || 106 ||
Furthermore, O sinless one, I shall proclaim another refutation of them to you: O King, they were established as the three castes because of their destruction of the poison of serpents. (107)
From that, the city of Camatkārapura came into being; moreover, the status of being "trijāta" (born of three) arose there specifically for all of them. || 108 ||
For these reasons, they have been excluded by Bhartṛyajña; furthermore, there is another reason why one does not attain purity even from their touch.
And he arrived at Kumbhakottha, which was inhabited by great Caṇḍālas.
The king said: "O Brahmin, please graciously tell me the cause of this; for you possess knowledge of the entire world, both the stationary and the moving. (111)
Viśvāmitra said: In this regard, I shall relate to you another ancient narrative concerning all those other excellent brahmins who were abandoned by Bhartṛyajña.
Formerly, in the city of Vardhamāna, there lived a man of the lowest caste, a Caṇḍāla named Kumbhaka, who was merciless and a performer of sinful deeds.
Then, after some time, a son was born to that Virūpa; though his father was deformed, the son was richly endowed with beauty due to the power of his past actions.
O King, he was tawny-eyed and very dark-complexioned, of middle age, skillful in all undertakings, and endowed with every auspicious mark. (115)

He quickly attains growth like the moon, the lord of stars, in the bright fortnight; likewise, as he is praised by all people, he possesses a beautiful form. Yet, constantly observing his family, he has attained supreme detachment.

Then, wandering here and there in distress from one country to another, he reached Camatkārapura, assuming the form of a twice-born. He bathed for all his religious rites and subsisted on food obtained through alms. || 117 ||
At that very time, O King, there was a brahmin of celebrated vows, renowned for his lineage in the Chāndogya school, named Subhadra.
There lived a city-dweller who performed sacrifices annually and was a master of the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences; to him was born a daughter with double rows of teeth.
Likewise, O King, she who has three breasts and is joined by a whorl on her back—whether one is poor, in great distress, or of low birth—[is still blessed]. (120)
No one accepts her even when she is being given away, for within six months she indeed devours her husband.

Those whose teeth are double this number—so say the experts in physiognomy (sāmudrikas)—and that maiden who has three breasts brings about the destruction of her father-in-law’s family; there is no doubt in this matter, therefore one should avoid her from afar.
She on whose body there is a whorl of hair on the back will quickly become unchaste; she is a practitioner of many evil deeds, therefore one should avoid her. || 123 ||
Then, seeing that prosperity attained, the brahmin Subhadraka mounted the wheel of anxiety and found no peace.
"What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can she obtain a husband? No one accepts her, even though she is entreated again and again. (125)
For even one who is poor, diseased, or old is indeed a Brāhmaṇa; since this was declared by the great seers in the past for the sake of a maiden in the Smṛti. (126)
A girl of eight years is Gaurī, one of nine years is Rohiṇī, and one of ten years is Kanyā; beyond that age, she is Rajasvalā (menstruating).
The mother, the father, and likewise the elder brother—these three go to hell upon seeing a daughter who has reached her menses. (128)
While he was reflecting thus, that outcaste, assuming the form of a twice-born, arrived at his house for alms and was seen by that high-souled man.
And having seen such a form, he was asked by him out of wonder: "O mendicant, from where have you come here, and where will you go? (130)
Having become one so highly destined, why have you adopted the *mādhukarī* (alms-gathering) way? Tell me, what is your lineage, and which is your most excellent [ancestral] branch? (131)
He said: "My place is in the Gauḍa country, very extensive, known by the name Bhojakaṭa, and inhabited by various brahmins. (132)
There lived a Brāhmaṇa named Mādhava, who had mastered the Vedas; he was renowned as belonging to the Vasiṣṭha lineage and was indicated by a single Pravara.
I am his son, known by the name Candraprabha.
Then, when I was established in the observance of vows in my eighth year, my father, who had mastered the Vedas, met his death.
My mother entered the fire along with him; thereupon, overcome by world-weariness, I departed from my own home.
Wandering here among the sacred fords (tīrthas), I have now arrived at your city; I shall now depart for the supreme holy field of Prabhāsa.

"O best of kings, it was there that the god Someśvara came, having left Kailāsa. Neither the Vedas nor the Śāstras have been studied by me; therefore, on the occasion of my pilgrimage, I wander for alms. (138)

Viśvāmitra said: Having heard those words of his, he reflected in his mind: "This man is a Brāhmaṇa from a noble region and possesses a most auspicious appearance; if he accepts my daughter, then I shall bestow her upon him. (139)
As long as she has not yet reached her menses, she is considered pure; this low-born woman quickly defiles my entire lineage, not just a single branch. (140)
Then, having consulted with his wife, he spoke to that Mleccha: "O twice-born one, if you will accept my daughter, I shall give her to you."
"I shall indeed always provide maintenance and nourishment for both of them. (142)
Having heard that, the outcaste was delighted and said to the best of kings: "I shall carry out your command; O King, grant me your daughter. (143)
Having said "So be it," he departed; by him his own daughter was given to him, and then the marriage was performed according to the procedure prescribed in the Gṛhya-sūtras.
Then, filled with satisfaction and considering himself to have achieved his purpose, he gave him wealth, grain, a house, a field, and cattle.
Then, having obtained her, he too indulged in many amorous diversions with foods, drinks, fine garments, perfumes, garlands, and ornaments.
He generally proceeds by whichever path he takes, while dogs indeed follow behind him, barking loudly. (147)

Just as it is for others born of the lowest castes, so it is especially for him; even if he is ever devoted to the study of the Vedas, the blood of that evil-minded one falls from his mouth at that very moment.
In the meantime, the entire world became apprehensive; approaching one another, they said, "This is undoubtedly a Caṇḍāla."
When these sons of a bitch went behind him barking, Subhadra too, having heard them, became lost in thought.
Believing that to be true, he was overcome with great sorrow, thinking: "Surely the husband of my daughter will be of the lowest caste."
It is known by all his actions that this person speaks as he does. || 152 ||
Thus, as that king brooded day and night, filled with concern over public scandal, how much time passed? (153)

When another day arrived, O best of the twice-born, each of those foremost brahmins, joined by the one standing in the center, came together at the abode of Brahmā and spoke for the sake of his purification, so that their doubt might be dispelled.
Then those best of the twice-born spoke to him, who was situated in the midst of the Brahma-throne, his face standing pale with its mouth turned inward.
Declare your family, your lineage, and your own specific *pravara*s; as well as the location and the country of the Brahmins, by which purity may be granted. (156)
Then, trembling and with a perspiring face, he spoke these words with downcast eyes, his hands joined in reverence, his voice faltering: || 157 ||
In the eighth year from my conception, my father passed away; thereafter, my devoted wife, my mother, took him with her and, leaving me behind in my grief and misery, entered the fire. 158.
Having attained detachment due to the sorrow of my father during my childhood, I set out on a pilgrimage to sacred fords along with other ascetics. (159)
"I have not studied the Veda, nor have I examined the Śāstras; devoted to pilgrimage, I have come to your city. (160)
"O Brahmins, I know this: that my father-in-law is of evil soul, being both Abhadra and Subhadra; and as for my lineage, it is indeed Vāsiṣṭha. (161)

Now, the land of Gauḍa is a region of singular excellence, with Madhupura as its capital. Then those Brāhmaṇas said: "For one whose lineage is not known, purification must be granted solely by means of the ordeal of the balance. (162)
Therefore, having ascended the balance solely for the sake of proving your Brahminhood, and having attained purification, you may then enjoy worldly pleasures while remaining right here. || 163 ||
Having committed this act of rashness, he said to all those best of the twice-born: "I accept whatever you desire, even a single heated māṣaka coin. (164)
I shall either enter the fire or consume poison. || 165 ||
How much more so, O Brahmins, would the performance of the water-pot ordeal bring happiness for the sake of a Brāhmaṇa? You have no compassion in your hearts toward me.

Then, O twice-born ones, those brahmins, having declared his purity resulting from the ordeal of the balance and having fixed the date following the day of the sun, all departed for their respective homes; and that outcaste, O brahmins, likewise returned to his own house.
Then, O best of kings, he spoke to his own wife in private: "I have been recognized by all the brahmins as being born of a low caste; I shall go to another country—come with me. (168)
The wife said: "I shall enter the fire; I will not go with you. O evil-minded one, I shall fall [into it], but I will not fall into the fires of hell. (169)
Awakened as I am, I shall not serve you, who have arisen from the lowest caste; for by you, this entire excellent place has been defiled with sin.
Likewise, my father’s palace belongs to one who performs the *prayāja* sacrifices for a year; therefore, go more swiftly before anyone finds out. (171)
If you do not abandon evil conduct, you will encounter great calamity. || 172 ||
Then, when nightfall arrived, covered only by a loincloth, he fled toward his desired direction out of fear for his life.
Viśvāmitra said: Then, when morning had arrived and the orb of the sun had risen, that daughter of the high-souled consecrated one [also appeared].
Wailing piteously, she approached her father and mother; with eyes clouded by tears, she spoke these words in a faltering voice.
"O father, O mother, what is this sin that you two have committed, that I have been given away to a wicked-souled outcaste? (3)
Having vanished at the onset of night and having made known my lineage to him, I shall therefore enter the blazing fire.
Having heard those words of hers, that consecrated Subhadraka fell motionless upon the ground like a tree broken by the wind.

Then, having been sprinkled repeatedly with cold water and quickly regaining consciousness with great difficulty while surrounded by his kinsmen, he uttered various lamentations, striking his own head again and again.
Then all those brahmins, defiled by contact with him, approached Bhartṛyajña and went along with him.
Accompanied by his daughter and Subhadra, who was endowed with modesty and discipline, he was settled in his own palace after his daughter had been given [in marriage].
In this world, there was a Caṇḍāla in the guise of a twice-born man, known by the name Candraprabha.
For as long as a year and a half, he was employed in rites for the gods and the ancestors; though a man of sinful deeds, he was not recognized, but now he has become manifest.
"O illustrious one, because of Subhadra, this entire place has been defiled by an outcaste; therefore, please exercise restraint over him. (11)
Some ate in his house and others likewise drank water; still others, having brought food to his home, offered it to him. || 12 ||
Or what is the use of saying much more to you, O best of the twice-born? There is no such person for whom the occurrence of that sin would not result in a mixture of castes.
O Mahāmati, this meritorious place was established by you in the past; indeed, you are the teacher of all. Therefore, tell us how purification is attained.
Then, after reflecting for a very long time upon many treatises on traditional law, he prescribed expiatory rites for all those twice-born men.
He bestowed upon Subhadra, who maintained the sacred fires, a hundred Cāndrāyaṇa penances, as well as the renunciation of all her household goods and the re-establishment of the fires.
The performance of a hundred-thousand-fold oblation (lakṣahoma) is prescribed for the purification of the interior of the house, and her entry into the fire is proclaimed for the sake of her son.
For as many meals as have been eaten by him in that man's house, for that many kṛcchra penances has he been told by that high-souled one.
O King, for as many measures of water as were drunk in that house, so many Prājāpatya penances were bestowed upon them.
For the Brahmins as well as for others residing in that place who have been defiled by contact with them, a Prājāpatya penance is prescribed for each individually.

For women and Śūdras, half of that [penance] is prescribed, and for children and the elderly, half of that again; furthermore, the total abandonment of earthen vessels has been declared [as the purification]. (21)

For all the worlds alike, there is likewise the renunciation of their essence; the Koṭihoma is prescribed for the station of Brahmā as previously described, solely by one who knows the stations, for the sake of purifying every station.
Then, raising his arm high, he spoke again to all those born of the city with a great, piercing cry: "O Brahmins! (23)
Subhadra must give his entire property to the Brahmins, as well as a fourth part of the wealth that was enjoyed in his house by those [who lived there]. (24)

Those by whom water was drunk from one-eighth part [of the vessel] receive the merit of a gift of a cow arising from that touch; for the remaining people as well, a sacrificial fee (dakṣiṇā) should be given according to their ability.
The initiated person should perform the recitation consisting of one hundred thousand *gāyatrīs*; the remaining brahmins should likewise perform the entire recitation according to their means. (26)
"And I myself, O best of the twice-born, shall perform three hundred breath-restraints daily, eating only at every sixth mealtime. (27)
Until the end of the year, purification will then occur for that evil-minded man; such was the state of him who had come into contact with people.
Having spoken thus, he then further addressed those best of the twice-born who were situated in the middle of the mouth, occupying the station of Brahmā.
From this day forward, whichever Nāgara gives his daughter in marriage to anyone who is not a Nāgara without first informing him, he shall become an outcast.
For he is unworthy of trust and excluded from the communal row, especially among the Nāgaras.
He who, having set aside the Nāgara śrāddha, bestows it upon another, his ancestors shall go away with their faces turned back, together with the gods.

He who performs the drinking of Soma without the Nāgara will undoubtedly be performing the drinking of liquor; likewise, he who performs the Śrāddha rite without his consent [will incur the same fault]. || 33 ||
Then everything of that person will become in vain, there is no doubt, who feeds a Nāgara devoid of purity. || 34 ||
"In the funeral rite (śrāddha), all of that for him as well shall become useless; this is the rule established by me for all the Nāgaras. (35)
Therefore, with every effort, the best of the twice-born should perform purification every year that arrives, for the sake of purifying their own abode. (36)

Viśvāmitra said: "O best of kings, all that I was asked by you has been told to you—how the Nāgaras became worthy of the Śrāddha rites, and how, in ancient times, Bhartṛyajña established their traditional boundaries. (37)
Viśvāmitra said: Then all those brahmins, having joined their palms in reverence and offered praise to the high-minded Bhartṛyajña, spoke these words. (1)
Regarding that which was stated by you: "The twice-born who has been purified is worthy of the Śrāddha rite, of a maiden in marriage, and of the drinking of Soma. (2)
Tell us everything regarding how purification should be performed for an entire city, as well as for one who has gone to another country.
For one born in another country, or again for one born there [in the land of the ancestors] whose paternal kin are unknown, who desires a common status— || 4 ||
Tell us all this in detail, O Mahāmati.
Viśvāmitra said: O best of kings, having heard those words of the brahmins, Bhartṛyajña spoke his own well-considered intention.
Bhartṛyajña said: This burden of questions that has been set forth by you is indeed great; nevertheless, having paid homage to the Self-Existent One (Svayambhū), I shall explain it.
He who, though having come from afar with his paternal lineage unknown, desires a share of the inheritance while proclaiming, "I am a Nāgara. (8)
His purification should be performed by eminent, tranquil, and auspicious twice-born men, having placed before them a Brahmin born at a sacred bathing-place (tīrtha) on a riverbank.
If the twice-born, whether out of desire, anger, hatred, or fear of falling from their status, do not grant purification to one who requests it; || 10 ||
The sin arising from the killing of a Brahmin accrues to all those present there; therefore, one who has arrived as a guest, especially even from afar, [should be honored].
The purification of that [sacrifice] must be diligently bestowed by the best of the twice-born; indeed, he has attained a threefold purification arising from my word.
He should be known as a pure Nāgara, even if born in other countries; first one should purify the paternal lineage, and then the maternal family is prescribed. (13)
Then, purified by these three, one through moral conduct (śīla) deserves the common stage. || 14 ||
When the end of the year has arrived, all Brahmins must diligently perform purification for the sake of purifying their own abodes.
For that purpose, at the end of autumn during the auspicious season, sixteen most excellent Brāhmaṇas, endowed with mastery of the four Vedas, should be appointed.
All the Brahmins present should be peaceful, self-controlled, and masters of their senses; among them, he should seat a Brahmin born at Gartatīrtha.
In front of that, four pedestals endowed with auspicious marks should be provided, arranged in four rows until the end of the month of Kārttika.
The first [recension] is for the sake of the Bahvṛca, another likewise for the Yājuṣa, another similarly for the Sāmaga, and the fourth for the Ādya.
Likewise, another fifth [mantra] is proclaimed for the purpose of the mudrā: the Śrīsūkta, the Pāvamāna, the Śākuna, and that which has Viṣṇu as its deity. || 20 ||
Likewise, the one learned in the Rigveda should recite the Pārāvata hymn together with the Jīvasūkta, as well as another hymn for the purpose of pacification.
The Śāntika, the Śivasaṃkalpa, and the Ṛṣikalpa—these four kinds [of hymns]—as well as the Maṇḍalabrāhmaṇa and the Gāyatrībrāhmaṇa.
Likewise, the Adhvaryu priest should recite the Puruṣasūkta and the Madhubrāhmaṇa there, as well as the five-limbed Rudra-mantras.
The Devavrata, the Gāyatra, the Somasūryavrata, and likewise up to the twenty-first, as well as another, the Rathantara. || 24 ||
The *Sauvratam*, the *Saṃhitā* of Viṣṇu, and likewise the *Jyeṣṭhasāman*, as well as the Rudras mentioned in the Sāmaveda joined with the Bhāruṇḍa Sāmans. (25)
There, the singer of the Sāmaveda (Chandoga) should recite whatever else may be propitiatory, as well as the Garbha Upaniṣad and the Skanda Sūkta.
Therein, one should first proclaim the Nīlarudras, the other Prāṇarudras, the Navarudras, and the Kṣurikas.
Then, amidst the proclamation of an auspicious day and the sounds of songs and musical instruments, he, wearing white garlands and garments and anointed with white sandalwood paste, [proceeded].
One desiring purification should go to where those brahmins are stationed; having bowed his head to them, he should then address the one seated in their midst.
"Indeed, you must request all these best of the twice-born on my behalf; since they shall grant me purification, you ought to show them favor. (30)
Then, for the sake of that purpose and for purification, the brahmin born at Garta-tīrtha, standing bowed with humility, should entreat the brahmins.
As he was clinging to a cow-hide, desiring purification, all those best of the twice-born were then questioned by him.
"This Nāgara twice-born man has arrived from afar for the sake of purification; if it pleases you, his purification should be granted. (33)
Then, by means of Vedic hymns, they must state either a prohibition or an injunction; this word of mine remains as it is, and cannot be spoken otherwise.
Then, O best of the twice-born, he saw many followers of the Ṛgveda and Yajurveda, as well as the Chāndogyas and others, in due order.

O best of the twice-born, if satisfaction arises in their minds, then [one should recite] hymns and words that are gentle, most auspicious, pertaining to Varuṇa and Indra, and originating from sources of blessing. (36)
The most excellent signs of mantras bring about prosperity and satisfaction; yet, if mental satisfaction does not arise from them, [what is the use]? (37)
At that time, the omens pertaining to Rudra, Yama, and especially Nirṛti, as well as those of Agni, were undesirable and likewise destructive. (38)

Now, if there should be any among them who are ignorant and not devoted to the recitation of the Vedas, then the offering of flowers must be addressed by those excellent brahmins once they have been satisfied. (39)
A hissing sound (sītkāra) should be made by those who are angry and devoid of contentment; likewise, no final decision should be made in any of these matters.
Just as ordinary men conduct themselves with common speech, so too, at the conclusion of the judicial decision, should the learned mediator act.
When the definitive conclusion has arisen for all, three claps of the hands should be properly given.

Thus ends the two hundred and first chapter, titled "The Description of the Resolution of the Nāgara's Question," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth section of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 201 ||
Viśvāmitra said: Having heard that, all the brahmins stood bowed with humility; O best of men, their minds filled with curiosity, they questioned him. (1)
A decision must be given by the best of the twice-born to a neutral party, setting aside human speech in favor of the words of the Veda.
Why should three claps of the hand be given by the great-souled one standing in the middle? Tell us all of this, for our curiosity is indeed great.
Having heard that, Bhartṛyajña spoke to those best of the twice-born: "Listen, I shall declare what the underlying cause is."
No word spoken by the citizens residing in the Brahma-shālā ever turns out to be untrue, whether it concerns something auspicious or inauspicious. (5)
Therefore, by means of the Vedic injunctions and the ritual libations (savanas), the best of the twice-born reveal to the petitioner who inquires whether his desired object will be attained or not.
Therefore, remaining impartial toward the twice-born, he should repeatedly ask him about the matter and its cause until a definitive resolution is reached.
If the word of those seated in the Brahma-assembly should become futile, their majesty perishes, and from that, anger arises.
From anger arises malice, and from malice comes the accumulation of sin; for this reason, O Brahmins, one who remains impartial is questioned repeatedly.
And just as the aggregate of all [the sounds] arises, then the one standing in the middle provides the three claps (tālatraya). || 10 ||
Among these, by the first [question] one destroys desire for those who provide answers; likewise, by the second one destroys anger, and by the third, greed.
For this reason, O twice-born ones, he should perform the three claps of the palms.
The Brāhmaṇas said: "The Ātharvaṇa is proclaimed as the fourth Veda; why then is it proclaimed as the first question for the Nāgaras?"
Bhartṛyajña said: O twice-born ones, since this first question concerning the Atharva was proclaimed by me, I shall explain it thoroughly; listen with well-composed minds. (14)
And in this case, one must certainly avoid envy, for it destroys one's own station; I have correctly explained this for the purification of one established in their proper place.

The sacrifices known as Agniṣṭoma and others, designated by the names Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman, proceed for the sake of the next world, as well as those pertaining to this world and those involving malevolent rites. (16)
And all that pertains to exorcism in the Atharvaveda was likewise spoken by Brahmā, the creator of the worlds, for the welfare of all people. (17)
The Atharvaveda should be studied first for the accomplishment of one's purpose; for this reason, although it is the fourth, it is established as the first.
O best of the twice-born, all this that I was asked by you has been narrated; for indeed, one should always perform every inquiry concerning a relationship as a single unified task.

Thus ends the two hundred and second chapter, titled "The Description of the Determination of Bhartṛyajña’s Words," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth section of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 202 ||
Ānarta said: "O twice-born one, tell me how a Nāgara, having come thus for the sake of purification and standing before the Nāgaras, attains that purity. (1)
Viśvāmitra said: || 1 ||
When the assembly has thus been established through the words of the mediator, he should be questioned: "Tell us, which of them is your mother? (2)
"What is her lineage? Who is her father, and what is remembered as her *pravara*? Having thus learned her ancestry, together with its *gotra* and *pravara*," ||| 3 ||
Then her mother must be questioned, and also the one who is her [mother]; and her own mother must also be questioned, and also the one who is her [mother]. || 4 ||
That too must be diligently understood by Brahmins in the performance of purificatory rites.
His father, grandfather, and likewise his great-grandfather—these three as well must be diligently purified for him.
Likewise, on the side of the paternal grandmother, these three are the best of the twice-born: the maternal grandfather, his father, and his father as well.
The mother, the maternal grandmother, and likewise any other preceding female ancestor, as well as the mother of the paternal grandmother—she too must be purified while accompanied by her husband.
Having thus understood the lineage of the branches in their entirety and in due order, one perceives its foundation extending from the root-lineage on all sides, like that of a banyan tree.
Then, purification should be performed with *sindūra* and *tilaka*, and after bestowing blessings in due order with the mantras of the four Vedas (*cātuścaraṇa*). || 10 ||

Then, O best of kings, the mediator should speak before him: "O King, having struck three claps of the hands, this Nāgara twice-born man is now purified; he has now become fit for the common status. (11)

Then, having gone to the fire-sanctuary and having gratified the sacrificial fire with the five-faced mantra, he should then offer the final oblation (pūrṇāhuti) and give sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) to the Brahmins according to his capacity, accompanied by a meal.
When the vermilion tilaka was applied before Brahmā at the word of the twice-born, the ancestors attained satisfaction, saying, "Today our lineage has been firmly established. (13)

If one's purity does not arise through the branches that reach down to the roots and the lineage, then that person, though worthy of being treated as a twice-born, must be subjected to restraint by the best of the twice-born.
Just as no other [birth] would arise for him, so his purity is ordained; thus purified, O Brahmin, he then becomes worthy of the śrāddha rite. || 15 ||

Moreover, what need is there to mention one born of the common eight families? Indeed, whatever śrāddha and other rites are performed by an impure Brāhmaṇa, all that becomes as futile as an oblation poured into ashes. || 16 ||
Therefore, with every effort, this Nāgara twice-born man must be purified for the sake of the purity of his own station as well as his own lineage. (17)

Thus ends the two hundred and third chapter, titled "Description of the Methods for the Purification of Nāgaras," in the Hāṭakeśvara-kṣetra-māhātmya of the Nāgara-khaṇḍa, within the sixth part of the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand verses. || 203 ||
Ānarta said: O Brahmin, O observer of noble vows, you have described to us in full detail the purity arising from the Nāgara lineage, just as you were asked.

Now, speak concerning one born of [doubtful] character who has lost his lineage—such a person who does not know his paternal grandfather nor his maternal grandmother, yet claims, "I am a Nāgara. How should his purification be performed? (2)
Viśvāmitra said: "In former times, Bhartṛyajña was questioned by the citizens regarding the loss of their lineage, O King, just as I have been questioned by you."
Bhartṛyajña said: If one whose lineage has been lost should declare in an assembly, "I am a Nāgara," his character must be thoroughly examined; thereafter, one may prescribe his purification. || 4 ||
If one always abides by those qualities and the exclusive legal conventions of the citizens, he may indeed be considered a citizen. (5)

O best of Brahmins, for the sake of his purification, the ordeal by balance (dhaṭa) should be administered; once he has attained purification through the balance, he shall then proceed to a state of purity.
He is worthy of ancestral rites (śrāddha), worthy of a maiden in marriage, and especially worthy of the Soma sacrifice; he is also fit for the common status in all ritual positions and duties.

All this that I was asked by you, O best of men, has been explained—namely, how purity arises for a twice-born man whose lineage has perished. Therefore, O great king, tell me what more you ought to hear.
Ānarta said: Therefore, having become Nāgaras, those Brahmins born of the eight families became the most excellent of all and remained preeminent in importance.
O Brahmin, is that power of theirs born of austerity, or arising from sacrifice, or perhaps produced by knowledge, or else originating from charity? (10)
Viśvāmitra said: "They are all endowed with virtues just like other citizens; moreover, there is another distinction regarding them: they were established by Śakra."
Therefore, they have attained the respect of all the twice-born.
Ānarta said: At what time, O high-minded one, were those Brahmins established here by Śakra? And for what purpose? Tell us this in detail. (13)
Viśvāmitra said: In ancient times, there was a preeminent Dānava known as Hiraṇyākṣa; he had a fierce battle with Śakra.
In that war between the gods and the asuras, O great king, many inhabitants of heaven and the dānavas died, each desiring to conquer the other. (15)
Then those Dānavas, struck down in battle by Śakra, were restored to life once more by Śukra through the power of his knowledge.
The gods have met their end and do not live by any means whatsoever; then, after some time, the slayer of Vṛtra spoke to Viṣṇu.
O Lord Janārdana, tell me of that destination which has been ordained for those who die at Dhārātīrtha by facing the blows [of battle].
O Acyuta, tell me also what kind of destiny awaits those who die with their faces turned away [from battle] and those who are intent on flight. (19)
Viṣṇu said: For those who die at Dhārātīrtha while facing the enemy in a great battle, there is no rebirth, just as there is none for seeds that have been destroyed.
Furthermore, O Lord of the Thirty-three, those who are struck on their backs while overcome by fear, and who are devoured by others, become pretas.

Indra said: "O Lord, some gods have died in battle while fighting face-to-face; likewise, others have been seen by me being slain while turning their backs. Will all the Dānavas attain the state of a ghost (preta), or not?"
Viṣṇu said: "O Thousand-eyed One, there is no doubt that all those who turn their backs in battle, whether they be gods or humans, go to the state of ghosts (pretas) once slain. (23)

O Lord of the Gods, for those who destroy their lineage, for those who commit suicide through that [poison], for those whose bodies are killed by fanged beasts or horned animals, and for those who die in the fire of poison, the state of a preta certainly arises; this is the truth, without a doubt. (24)
Indra said: "O Lord, how may their liberation from this dreadful state of being a ghost (preta) occur? Tell me all of this, so that I may apply myself to the effort. (25)

The Blessed Lord said: O Lord of the Gods, for them the Śrāddha ceremony is joined [with great merit] when the sun is situated in Virgo, on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Nabhasya.
If they go to Gayā with devotion, according to the word of the Grandfather (Brahmā), then they attain liberation; this is the truth, without a doubt. (27)
Indra said: "O Madhusūdana, why is the śrāddha performed on that day for those slain by weapons? Tell me everything in detail. (28)

The Blessed Lord said: Formerly, when that day had arrived, Śambhu was entreated by the Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, Kūṣmāṇḍas, and even the Rākṣasas: "O God, today for one day, while the sun is situated in the sign of Virgo... (29)
"Give to us so that there may be satisfaction for a year; show compassion toward the poor when the Śrāddha is offered by those born of our lineage. (30)

The Blessed Lord said: "Whoever, born of this lineage, shall perform a śrāddha on this day when it has arrived—the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight of the month of Nabhasya—there will be supreme satisfaction [for the ancestors] for the duration of an entire year."
Furthermore, whoever born in your lineage shall go to Gayā and perform the śrāddha ceremony in that manner, by him you shall attain liberation.
